articles.title: Switzerland Confirms AI-Assisted Cyberattacks Breached Critical Infrastructure Operators
articles.text:
Attackers using AI agents have broken into computer systems at Swiss organizations in four of five confirmed attacks, the first such cases in the country, the country's cybersecurity agency said yesterday.
Three of the attacks targeted critical infrastructure operators, and two of those succeeded, with no major disruptions reported. The victims have not been named, and it is not known who is behind the attacks.
Florian Schütz, who directs Switzerland's National Cyber Security Centre, gave the figures in an interview with public broadcaster SRF.
All five cases were reported in recent days. Small and medium-sized companies were among the organizations hit, and they came forward voluntarily.
The agency's first notice, a security advisory published on Tuesday, said the agents had compromised the victims' IT systems in every case known at that point. Neither the notice nor yesterday's broadcast interview explains why the count changed.
"These cases represent a shift in the cyber threat landscape," the advisory said.
The targeted operators are in at least two sectors. Electricity, drinking water, and telecommunications suppliers are examples of what Switzerland counts as critical infrastructure, according to a news agency report on the interview.
The attacks involve what the Swiss agency calls agentic offensive frameworks, AI agents that find security weaknesses and carry out attacks on their own. Its advisory named ARTEX and CyberStrikeAI as examples of agents reachable over the internet, not as the tools used in the five cases.
The agents are often used to scan for known, unpatched weaknesses and can run many attacks in parallel, the agency says. When defenses respond, the agents switch methods, leaving companies significantly less time to detect an intrusion and respond.
The number of AI attack tools freely reachable online has nearly doubled since October, according to the agency. The figure counts available tools, not attacks or victims.
Raphael Reischuk, co-founder of Switzerland's National Test Institute for Cybersecurity, expects a larger wave of attacks and says companies underestimate the risk.
Italy's national computer security incident response team, CSIRT Italia, described mass compromise campaigns in an official bulletin this week. In the cases it observed firsthand, AI-directed autonomous agents broke into a large number of systems within a few hours.
The agents adapt their actions within seconds, run in parallel without human input, and chain vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, and compromised credentials together, the bulletin says. It names ARTEX, CyberStrikeAI, PentAGI, and DeepSeek Harness, an open-source agent whose Red Team Mode uses a built-in prompt to get past the underlying model's safety limits.
Each action on its own looks like normal user or API traffic. Detection depends on context: where requests come from, how often they arrive, how much data moves, and the order in which things happen.
Britain's National Cyber Security Centre reported the same pattern in agency guidance this week. "Since September 2026, the NCSC has seen a marked rise in AI-assisted cyber attacks," it said.
Some incidents caused downtime on internet-facing services, and others gave attackers a foothold for further agent-driven activity. The weaknesses are old ones: credentials committed to code repositories, misconfigured infrastructure-as-code, default or missing authentication, and weaknesses in APIs.
What has changed is the speed, persistence, and low cost of the attacks, the British agency says. The frameworks are also noisy, which makes them easier to detect.
The European Commission has already been hit. Attackers using ARTEX broke into its human resources, medical reimbursement, and translation systems, the Commission has confirmed, in an earlier intrusion first detected on October 22.
What Defenders Should Do
The strongest common advice from the three agencies is to shrink the time attackers have. Their recommendations overlap:
- Install critical security updates on internet-facing systems within 24 hours of release (Switzerland), and patch flaws already being exploited first (Italy).
- Disconnect or isolate internet-facing systems that cannot be patched quickly (Italy).
- Reduce what is reachable from the internet, using geo-blocking, allow lists, and authentication in front of services (Switzerland, UK).
- Require MFA or passkeys on everything reachable from the internet, and grant the lowest privileges that work (Switzerland).
- Watch for unusual behavior and data volumes (Switzerland), and correlate logs: agent activity shows up as bursts of requests and high error rates (UK).
- Put bot challenges on high-value endpoints, and use decoys such as honeytokens to catch and slow agents (UK).
- Load Italy's published indicator feeds into monitoring tools, noting that the indicators change quickly and are valid only for their stated timeframes (Italy).

articles.text:
Histórico: Huawei Watch Fit 5 Pro atinge 58% OFF na Black e é destaque da marca
Watch Fit 5 Pro tem corpo de titânio e sensores avançados; smartphone da Huawei sai 58% mais em conta no prazo com cupom no Mercado Livre
O Watch Fit 5 Pro está saindo por R$ 849 em até 10x sem juros com cupom ACABANDO no Mercado Livre. O novo smartwatch premium da Huawei, com corpo de titânio e tela AMOLED de 1,92″, alcança o menor preço histórico na Black Friday 2026, com desconto de 58% sobre o original de R$ 1.999.
Esta oferta é o menor preço que já encontramos para o Huawei Watch Fit 5 Pro. Nas outras 10 ofertas publicadas desde julho de 2026, o melhor foi R$ 962 (Mercado Livre, 25/11/2026).
O Watch Fit 5 Pro é um dos melhores smartwatches da Huawei, capaz de monitorar mais de 100 atividades esportivas diferentes. Ele conta com monitores de frequência cardíaca e ritmo em corridas, e função de mini treino para exercícios localizados, além de monitores do sono, estresse e oxigenação do sangue (SpO2).
Sua ampla tela AMOLED de 1,92″ possui taxa de 60 Hz e brilho de até 3.000 nits, entregando fluidez acima da média na categoria e imagens com cores vibrantes, além de garantir a visibilidade em qualquer lugar.
Este wearable possui sensores de queda capazes de detectar uma emergência médica e, caso o usuário não se recupere dentro de um determinado tempo, ele dispara alertas para contatos selecionados e números como 190 (polícia) e 192 (ambulância), desde que esteja pareado a um celular.
O corpo em liga de titânio de grau aeroespacial do Watch Fit 5 Pro traz ainda um vidro de Safira 2.5D sobre a tela, resistente contra pancadas e quedas. Ele conversa tanto com iPhone quanto com Android, oferecendo versatilidade no uso.
Sua bateria de 471 mAh tem autonomia de até 10 dias, segundo a empresa. A certificação IP6X garante proteção contra poeira, mas o acessório não tem defesa documentada contra água; a fabricante, no entanto, informa que ele resiste a até 5 ATM.
O Huawei Watch Fit 5 Pro (R$ 849 em até 10x sem juros com cupom ACABANDO) possui conectividade Bluetooth 6.0 e GPS multibanda, que determina a posição do usuário em tempo real.

Dust buildup is one of the leading causes of overheating PCs, so whether you have a basic laptop you got on sale for under $300 or a high-end desktop PC costing thousands of dollars, it’s a good idea to invest in a machine that could help you keep it clean. This is where the MiaEpic Z3 comes in, which is currently on sale at $28.49, giving you a 29% discount and saving you $11.50 from its original price. Even though it may be cheaper than some of the options that you could find on Amazon, it can reach speeds of up to 280,000 RPM, allowing it to blow dust and other debris from your fans, filters, and other PC components with little effort. It also comes with enough battery power to run continuously for 90 to 150 minutes, while sporting a fast-charging USB-C port that can take it from flat empty to full in about three hours. articles.title: Cómo solucionar problemas de sonido de los stickers con audio en WhatsApp y qué ajustes revisar
articles.text:
WhatsApp incorpora una nueva función que permite enviar stickers acompañados de sonidos, grabaciones de voz y otros archivos de audio. Sin embargo, algunos usuarios tienen dificultades para escuchar estos contenidos porque, a diferencia de los mensajes de voz, no se reproducen automáticamente cuando llegan a una conversación.
Para activar el sonido es necesario realizar una acción desde el propio sticker y comprobar que el celular tenga habilitada la reproducción multimedia.
La herramienta, conocida como Sound Stickers, busca ampliar las posibilidades de comunicación dentro de la aplicación de mensajería. Su funcionamiento permite combinar imágenes estáticas o animadas con pequeños clips de sonido, lo que abre la posibilidad de compartir expresiones, efectos y mensajes personalizados sin necesidad de enviar una nota de voz tradicional.
Si un sticker llega a una conversación, pero no se escucha, no necesariamente significa que WhatsApp tenga un problema. Primero es importante identificar cómo se activa el audio y revisar algunos ajustes del teléfono que pueden impedir su reproducción.
Cómo escuchar los stickers con audio de WhatsApp
Los stickers con sonido tienen un funcionamiento diferente al de los mensajes de voz. Cuando llegan a un chat, el audio permanece silenciado inicialmente para evitar que se reproduzca de manera inesperada, especialmente en conversaciones grupales.
Para escucharlos, el usuario debe seguir estos pasos:
- Abrir la conversación: ingresar al chat individual o grupal donde recibió el sticker.
- Identificar el símbolo de sonido: observar si aparece un pequeño ícono de altavoz tachado o que indica que el audio está silenciado.
- Activar la reproducción: tocar el sticker o el símbolo de sonido para iniciar el contenido.
- Esperar unos segundos: el audio se reproduce junto con la animación y puede repetirse hasta tres veces antes de detenerse.
No es necesario descargar otra aplicación ni modificar una configuración especial de WhatsApp para escuchar estos contenidos. La reproducción manual forma parte del funcionamiento de los Sound Stickers.
Qué hacer si los stickers de audio no se escuchan
Si el usuario ya pulsó el ícono de sonido y todavía no puede escuchar el contenido, existen varios ajustes del celular que conviene revisar. En algunos casos, el problema está relacionado con el volumen o con la conexión de dispositivos externos.
1. Subir el volumen multimedia. Los teléfonos suelen separar el volumen de las llamadas, las notificaciones y los contenidos multimedia. Por eso, es importante utilizar los botones laterales y comprobar que se esté aumentando el volumen de reproducción de videos, música y otros archivos.
2. Revisar el modo silencio. Algunos dispositivos cuentan con interruptores físicos o configuraciones que limitan la reproducción de sonidos. Conviene comprobar que el teléfono no tenga activado un modo que impida escuchar el contenido.
3. Desconectar los auriculares Bluetooth. Si el celular está conectado a unos audífonos inalámbricos, un parlante u otro dispositivo, el sonido podría estar reproduciéndose allí y no en el altavoz del teléfono.
4. Cerrar y volver a abrir WhatsApp. Salir de la aplicación y ejecutarla nuevamente puede solucionar errores temporales que afectan la reproducción de archivos multimedia.
5. Actualizar la aplicación. Es recomendable ingresar a Google Play Store o App Store y comprobar si existe una versión más reciente de WhatsApp. Una actualización puede corregir fallos, aunque no garantiza que todas las novedades estén disponibles para cada cuenta.
También se puede pedir a otro contacto que envíe un sticker con audio. De esta manera, será posible comprobar si el inconveniente ocurre con un contenido específico o con todos los stickers que llegan a la conversación.
Por qué algunos usuarios todavía no pueden utilizar esta función
Si después de revisar los ajustes del teléfono el problema continúa, existe otra posibilidad: la función todavía no está habilitada en todas las cuentas de WhatsApp.
Según los reportes de WABetaInfo, los Sound Stickers comenzaron a aparecer para algunos usuarios de la versión beta 2.26.47.1 de WhatsApp para Android y de TestFlight 26.46.10.70 para iOS. Su distribución es gradual, por lo que actualizar la aplicación no significa que todas las personas puedan acceder inmediatamente a las mismas herramientas.
Además, hay una diferencia entre recibir y crear estos stickers. Un usuario puede recibirlos, reproducirlos, guardarlos en favoritos y reenviarlos, aunque todavía no tenga habilitada la opción para producir sus propios contenidos con sonido.
Por eso, si no aparece el ícono correspondiente en el editor de stickers, lo más probable es que deba esperar a que WhatsApp active la característica en su cuenta. No es necesario reinstalar la aplicación ni recurrir a programas externos para intentar habilitarla.

articles.title: iPhone 18 : du retard dans la production. Et aussi au lancement ?
articles.text:
Apple a prévu de sortir ses nouveaux iPhone 18 dans les premiers mois de 2027. Mais il y a des problèmes à l'allumage au niveau de la production !
Apple a cette année fait le pari de diviser la sortie de ses iPhone, avec en premier les iPhone 18 Pro qui ont été lancés seuls lors de la keynote de rentrée, en compagnie du téléphone pliable iPhone Duo. Les iPhone 18 de base eux doivent être lancés au début de l'année 2027. Un plan qui ne semble pas marcher sans accroc pour Apple !
La production en masse des iPhone 18 repoussée
Il y a un peu de retard chez Apple. C'est ce que nous apprend le leaker chinois Fixed Focus Digital, et dont Macrumors se fait l'écho. En effet, d'après ce dernier, ni l'iPhone 18, ni l'iphone 18e, ne sont encore entrés en production de masse.
Et ce n'est pas le premier retard. Il y en avait déjà eu un qui avait fait passé cette production de masse d'octobre à la fin novembre. Cette fois, cette étape est encore repoussée selon les informations du leaker, au nouvel an.
Apple aura peu de stock pour une sortie au premier trimestre 2027
Apple se trouvera donc dans une position plus compliquée, avec assez peu de temps pour accumuler du stock pour son lancement. Car il faut le rappeler, la marque à la pomme croquée compte normalement lancer ses prochains iPhone soit au mois de février, soit au mois de mars - selon des informations du journaliste de Bloomberg Mark Gurman. De quoi pousser Apple à retarder l'officialisation ?
Pour rappel, on s'attend à ce que ces modèles soient assez similaires. Le même leaker a notamment dernièrement mis en ligne sur Weibo un document qui laisse entendre que les deux appareils auraient droit à un écran de 6,3 pouces, et à une batterie de 4 430 mAh. Ils intégreraient aussi une puce A20, avec une RAM que certaines rumeurs indiquent légèrement à la hausse, à 9 Go.
Source : Macrumors

articles.title: Unpatched Cacti Zero-Day Enables RCE in Just Four HTTP Requests via Guest Access
articles.text:
Details have emerged about a new zero-day vulnerability in Cacti, an open-source network monitoring tool, that could be exploited to achieve remote code execution.
The proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit, which has yet to be assigned a CVE identifier, has been tracked as 4HTTP2SHELL and 4HTTP2ROOT.
"I found a path from a fresh, unauthenticated HTTP session to command execution as the Cacti server user in four requests," a security researcher who goes by the online alias "ek0ms savi0r" said. "No login. No valid API key. No phishing. Just four HTTP requests against the default guest surface."
The shortcoming affects Cacti Core 1.2.31, the latest version, when the guest account is enabled. It's worth noting that the guest account is disabled by default starting with Cacti version 0.8.7.
At a high level, the vulnerability allows an attacker to abuse the guest access to write an unvalidated value (i.e., non-numeric text) into a setting called "preview_graphs_per_page" via "auth_profile.php?action=update_data." The configuration parameter controls how many graphs are displayed per page when viewing graphs in Preview Mode.
The crafted value takes the form of arbitrary SQL strings that can be turned into a second-order SQL injection by taking advantage of the fact that Cacti does not validate that the user-provided input is actually an integer value. This, in turn, opens the door for arbitrary SQL query execution when the graph preview page ("graph_view.php") is loaded with default filters.
The SQL query demonstrated by "ek0ms savi0r" is an UPDATE statement to modify a record in Cacti's poller table. In the final stage of the attack, the realtime poller endpoint ("graph_realtime.php") is invoked from the same guest session, which causes the modified row from the poller table to be read and passed as input to PHP's popen() function without any allowlist or sanitization checks.
The researcher has pointed out four failures that ultimately make it possible to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution -
- The guest can write a numeric setting as an arbitrary string
- The stored default bypasses request validation
- Cacti's PHP PDO database driver accepts stacked statements through the SQL LIMIT clause
- The poller executes a database-stored command string
Successful exploitation of the flaw can allow an attacker to compromise the Cacti server and provide a pivot point to the target network as it exposes sensitive data, or even suppress alerts by modifying the poller table.
"Because Cacti often stores credentials and connection details for routers, switches, servers, and other devices across a network, an attacker who reaches this level of command execution can gain a foothold reaching far beyond the monitoring server itself," watchTowr said in an advisory.
In the absence of a fix, users are advised to disable the guest account and restrict access to the Cacti web interface to mitigate potential risks. It's also essential to review poller configuration entries for unexpected command values and apply the fixes as soon as they become available.

articles.title: Un truco permite jugar GTA 6 a 40 FPS en PS5, aunque provocaría estos daños
articles.text:
Los jugadores de Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) encontraron una manera de superar el límite de 30 fotogramas por segundo (FPS) en PlayStation 5 mediante modificaciones no oficiales. Las pruebas realizadas en una PS5 Slim muestran que el videojuego puede alcanzar alrededor de 40 FPS de media al reducir la resolución gráfica, aunque el procedimiento también eleva las temperaturas de la consola por encima de los 90 °C.
El experimento fue compartido por el usuario gama224 en Reddit. Los resultados muestran que es posible conseguir una experiencia más fluida sin necesidad de cambiar de consola, pero también exponen los riesgos de modificar los parámetros de funcionamiento del equipo.
La modificación requiere una consola con jailbreak, es decir, con un sistema alterado que permite ejecutar herramientas y aplicaciones no autorizadas por Sony. Por tanto, no se trata de una opción disponible para todos los propietarios de PS5 ni de una configuración oficial de Rockstar Games.
Cómo conseguir 40 FPS en GTA 6 en una PS5 Slim
El procedimiento consiste en desbloquear el límite de fotogramas por segundo que mantiene el juego y reducir la resolución interna para disminuir la carga de trabajo de la tarjeta gráfica. De esta manera, la consola necesita procesar menos píxeles y puede dedicar más recursos a mantener una frecuencia de imagen elevada.
Según las mediciones publicadas por gama224, cuando la escala de resolución se establece en el 50 % de una imagen 4K, equivalente a 1.920 × 1.080 píxeles, GTA 6 alcanza entre 35 y 40 FPS en zonas urbanas con muchos elementos. En escenarios acuáticos, donde la exigencia gráfica es diferente, el rendimiento sube hasta los 45-50 FPS.
Al aumentar la escala al 60 %, equivalente aproximadamente a 2.304 × 1.296 píxeles, los resultados son más modestos. Las áreas urbanas se mantienen entre 30 y 35 FPS, mientras que los escenarios acuáticos llegan a los 40 FPS.
El punto de equilibrio de las pruebas se encuentra alrededor del 55 % de escala de resolución, unos 2.112 × 1.188 píxeles. Con esta configuración, el videojuego registra aproximadamente 40 FPS de media, con variaciones entre 35 y 45 FPS.
Sin embargo, el rendimiento depende del escenario. Las zonas con mayor tráfico, personajes y actividad pueden exigir más recursos del procesador, por lo que reducir la resolución no garantiza mantener una frecuencia constante.
La temperatura de la PS5 supera los 90 grados
El principal inconveniente de estas pruebas aparece en el apartado térmico. El usuario informó que su PS5 Slim suele registrar temperaturas cercanas a los 80 °C con la configuración original de GTA 6. Al desbloquear los FPS, las mediciones superaron los 90 °C, pudiendo ocasionar daños a la consola.
Para controlar esta situación, recurrió a una aplicación homebrew que permite establecer un objetivo térmico de 85 °C mediante ajustes en la ventilación de la consola. No obstante, no se especificó qué sensor proporcionaba las temperaturas registradas ni cuáles eran las condiciones ambientales durante las pruebas.
También existen testimonios de otros participantes que aseguran haber conseguido temperaturas inferiores con diferentes configuraciones de ventilación. Sin embargo, estas experiencias no permiten establecer un comportamiento general para todas las PS5 Slim o PS5 Pro.
Rockstar no ha anunciado un modo oficial de 40 FPS
Las pruebas resultan relevantes porque GTA 6 mantiene un objetivo de 30 FPS en las consolas de Sony. Una frecuencia de 40 FPS permitiría una animación más fluida, especialmente en televisores compatibles con frecuencias de actualización de 120 Hz.
La diferencia se aprecia en el tiempo que permanece cada fotograma en pantalla: a 30 FPS, cada imagen dura aproximadamente 33,3 milisegundos; a 40 FPS, ese intervalo baja a 25 milisegundos.
Pese a estos resultados, Rockstar Games no ha anunciado un modo oficial de 40 FPS para PlayStation 5. Las modificaciones tampoco garantizan estabilidad ni conservan necesariamente la calidad gráfica prevista para el juego.
Por ahora, el experimento demuestra que es posible superar los 30 FPS mediante ajustes no oficiales, pero también deja en evidencia las limitaciones del hardware. Intentar reproducirlo implica asumir riesgos que no están respaldados por Sony ni por Rockstar.

articles.title: From fan heaters to thermal socks, 12 winter warmers under £40 to keep you cosy this Black Friday — recommended by a chilly person
articles.text:
Do you always feel chilly? Are you trying to avoid putting the heating on? I hear you, so I'm sharing my secrets to staying snug without touching the thermostat — and they're all going cheap in the Black Friday sales.
Number one on my list is the Beurer Electric Fleece Heat Pad for £21.50 at Argos (was £43), which sits on my lap in the office throughout the winter — and much of the spring and autumn as well. It's less conspicuous than putting on your coat indoors, is silent, and has passed office electrical inspections year after year.
Heat Holders gloves and socks are excellent thanks to their soft fleece linings, and if you're particularly cold indoors, there are several fingerless and convertible styles that mean you can still hold your mouse and type while wearing them. There are heaps, so take a look at all the Heat Holders deals at Amazon.

articles.title: ThreatsDay: 10M NGINX Services at Risk, 250+ Malicious Extensions, AI Server Hijacking + 17 More Stories
articles.text:
A website can look perfectly fine to the person running it. Log out, visit the same page, and things might look different. Something similar is happening with browser extensions, where even the way you find and install one can change what it does. Checking whether software works as expected only tells you so much.
Then there’s the question of who gets to use what. Stolen logins are opening doors across connected systems, while some AI servers are sitting online for anyone to use at someone else’s expense. Even software responsible for keeping the power on has found its way into an attack.
Meanwhile, authorities are taking down large scam operations, extortion gangs are making comebacks, and ransomware activity is picking up. Some of the more worrying findings this week involve things most people would have little reason to suspect. The details are worth a look.
The threats change every week. Subscribe, and we’ll alert you when each new ThreatsDay Bulletin is out.
- 
  
  Stolen credentials expose customer data Todoist has disclosed that an attacker gained unauthorized access to its production systems and retrieved some customer information on November 23, 2026. The incident affects 6% of its users. "Between November 22 and 23, an attacker used a stolen credential associated with our version control system to modify automated workflows in three repositories and obtain additional credentials," it said. During this time, they could also read our source code. Our investigation found no changes to application code. One of the credentials they obtained allowed them to change how employees access our internal systems. The attacker used it to take over an employee’s work account and gain access to our cloud infrastructure. On November 23, the attacker downloaded a file containing account information for some early Todoist users whose passwords were stored using an older hashing method. They also made targeted queries for account tokens, searched some customer content for credentials, and accessed email information through connected Todoist for Outlook accounts."
- 
  
  Record cybersecurity acquisition CrowdStrike said it will acquire Zscaler in a deal worth $43.9 billion, making it the biggest cybersecurity acquisition on record. "Security used to be about keeping the adversary out. Today, safety is required to let AI in," CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz said. "The network used to connect people to places. Now it connects agents to data. With Zscaler, we're building cybersecurity's operating system: a single control plane to deploy AI, control AI, and enable any agentic application to run safely. We see a path to become the largest AI safety and security company the world has ever seen."
- 
  
  Paid ads activate hidden payloads Microsoft's Edge Extensions Security Team has documented SleeperWidget, a set of over 250 extensions across Microsoft Edge Add-ons, Chrome Web Store, and Mozilla Add-ons that work as advertised unless installed through a paid search ad. Once installed that way, they collect browsing data, inject ads, and change shopping links. "Its extensions pose as maps, recipe finders, package trackers, and other everyday tools. Most deliver the features they advertise, which makes hidden behavior easier to miss," it said. "In the extensions we analyzed, installation through a paid-advertising funnel also activated browsing-data collection, ad injection, and shopping-link modification."
- 
  
  LLMjacking without exploits An analysis of 20,354 internet-facing hosts has revealed that thousands of servers where AI services or notebook APIs have been deployed and left accessible without authentication, potentially enabling attackers to abuse them for their own purposes. "More than half of the exposed Ollama servers in this scan have already been touched by someone who is not the owner," Rapid7 said. "79% of exposed Ollama hosts list at least one :cloud model, mostly GLM, DeepSeek, MiniMax and Kimi variants. An exposed, signed-in server can provide access to someone else's paid subscription, with the bill landing on the owner. This is the self-hosted version of LLMjacking, and it requires no exploit at all."
- 
  
  Blockchain-backed malware delivery SonicWall Capture Labs has disclosed details of a Java-based loader from SilentNet, a Java-based remote access trojan and infostealer sold as a malware-as-a-service offering that's advertised on YouTube. The JAR masquerades as a mod for Minecraft Fabric and targets players who download mods from external sources. "Once loaded by the game, it pulls the player's Minecraft session token from memory. It then gets its command-and-control (C2) address from a smart contract on the Polygon blockchain, and downloads a portable Python runtime hidden inside a PNG image to run a second-stage infostealer," SoniWall said. "Every string in the JAR is hidden by per-character arithmetic; it resolves hostnames through DNS-over-HTTPS, and it talks to its C2 through a custom HTTPS client that skips certificate validation."
- 
  
  AI-powered phishing infrastructure Threat actors are using DeepSite, Hugging Face's AI website builder, to create dozens of phishing and credential-stealing pages on Hugging Face Spaces impersonating 28 brands, including Microsoft, Google, PayPal, Chase, and Coinbase. "29 of the pages were built with DeepSite, Hugging Face’s AI website builder," Aikido said. "One Microsoft login clone took about 90 minutes of plain-language prompts, and other operators asked the builder to hide their pages from crawlers or send stolen logins to Telegram."
- 
  
  Credential theft spans 127 CVEs According to VulnCheck, requests to steal credentials made up 13% of all vulnerability exploitation recorded between January and November 2026. Credential-harvesting attempts appeared across 127 of 694 CVEs observed in its honeypot network, with open-source software and AI developer tools like Apache, Laravel, Langflow, Flowise, MLflow, and n8n taking up 61% of the CVEs associated with credential-harvesting attempts. "Attackers search application files, logs and environment variables for database passwords, cloud credentials and API keys, with file-read and SSRF vulnerabilities providing opportunities without code execution," VulnCheck said, adding it "observed 1,756 attempts targeting AI provider and coding agent credentials from 406 IP addresses across 27 CVEs."
- 
  
  Ransomware disrupts critical services A previously unknown ransomware and data-extortion group calling itself BYOD has claimed at least nine organizations between October 5 and November 9, 2026. "Its attacks have had real-world consequences, including ambulance diversion, more than 30 clinics closed, and campus-wide device shutdowns," TrendAI said. "BYOD runs a pressure campaign alongside the intrusion: audio messages on infected computers, public leak-site posts, statements framing its attacks as holding organizations accountable, and outreach to individual victims." Although the complete intrusion chain remains to be analyzed, evidence points to credential compromise and a remote access trojan on an employee's computer for initial access.
- 
  
  Malicious JavaScript delivery platform A malware campaign has been observed installing a fake WordPress plugin built almost entirely by a name generator, including its title, directories, files, and functions (e.g., trijavascriptly, ultravueal, maxdataic, and quadmicroservicesion). "Behind the generated names is a second-stage delivery platform that runs arbitrary JavaScript in the browser of every anonymous visitor to an infected site, routes that traffic through the victim's own domain, and lies dormant for logged-in users," Wordfence said. The malware has been discovered twice, once in January 2026 and another in September 2026. Exactly how the plugin is installed is not known, but investigation shows that it's likely via a compromise of an administrator account.
- 
  
  Global scam networks disrupted The U.S. Department of Justice (DoJ) has announced that over 17.3 million scam accounts have been deplatformed on Meta, 700 fraudulent crypto investment websites seized, and 12 U.S. arrest warrants issued as part of efforts to tackle foreign and domestic scams over the past six months. The Strike Force has traced and restrained $1,082,260,156.82 in cryptocurrency stolen from U.S. victims. "Our Scam Center Strike Force has continued its work investigating cyber-enabled fraud perpetrated against Americans by transnational organized crime groups, emanating out of Asia and attacking America's main street," said U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro. "The Strike Force teams focus on identifying and pursuing key leaders — including Chinese organized crime affiliates operating in Cambodia, Laos, and Burma, and rapidly expanding around the globe — to bring them to justice." FBI Director Kash Patel said the Operation Blackout scam demolition initiative has "seized nearly $17 billion in illicit funds, taken more than 14,000 digital devices, directly warned over 11,000 Americans from scam attempts, and prevented more than $690 million in potential victim losses." Over 29 scam compounds operating across Asia, Africa, and the Middle East have been dismantled and more than 2,200 trafficked workers have been repatriated. The U.S. State Department has also worked with U.S. and Southeast Asian law enforcement to facilitate the freezing of more than $1 billion in stolen cryptocurrency, the takedown of over 1.4 million fraudulent websites and accounts, and several arrests. Earlier this month, the U.S. Attorney's Office also filed a civil forfeiture action to recover 456,602 USDT (Tether) that's alleged to be proceeds of romance fraud schemes targeting individuals in Massachusetts and elsewhere on online dating sites and Facebook.
- 
  
  Billion-dollar crypto recovery bid The Justice Department has filed a civil action to recover over $1.1 billion in cryptocurrency that was illicitly obtained from Binance by North Korean actors in a major hack last month. "To date, the United States has assisted in the freezing, seizing, and/or the return of almost $3 billion worth of cryptocurrency from multiple sources since the theft from Binance on or about October 29," the DoJ said. Brett Leatherman, Cyber Branch Operations Director of the FBI, said, "North Korea depends on sophisticated laundering techniques to convert stolen cryptocurrency into funds that support the regime's illicit activities," adding, "Following the Binance theft, the FBI and our partners moved quickly to trace and freeze stolen assets and share critical information with virtual asset service providers."
- 
  
  Extortion gang resurfaces after arrests The ShinyHunters extortion gang claims to have returned on a new data leak site following a series of arrests targeting alleged members. The new TOR site, launched on November 23, features messages in both Russian and English announcing the group's return, while denouncing a former member, Rey (aka Saif), who was reportedly arrested and is "actively cooperating" with law enforcement. "We want to let you know that from now on we will only be using our account on Exploit, which we've held since 2020," the group said. "We won't be active on any other BF-style forums anymore." They also concluded the statement with a shout-out to two other arrested members, Umbreon and Ed Dubrovsky. "Thank you for being with us all this time," the group said. "We won't forget you, and we might even send you a couple of postcards to your rat-infested cells. It was a pleasure working with you. And it's truly a shame that our guys got caught because of such silly mistakes, ones that could easily have been avoided if you fools hadn't gotten involved with the wrong people."
- 
  
  AI misuse detection without data retention Anthropic has launched a public beta of Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS), allowing organizations to detect potentially harmful AI activity across multiple interactions while maintaining zero data retention (ZDR). The protection employs a second defensive layer, known as automated safety monitoring, that looks for patterns of misuse across multiple requests to provide automated safety monitoring without storing any customer data. "Instead, our automated safety monitoring system analyzes data stored entirely on infrastructure controlled by our customers," Anthropic said. "When automated safety monitoring finds a risk, it creates a Safety Case for you to review. These cases can be read from your cloud storage or through an API, and can be integrated with security information and event management systems. They do not include inputs and outputs. Once it's set up, automated safety monitoring can help your team detect intentional misuse that could lead to serious harm (like offensive cyber operations). It can also help detect agents that take actions beyond a user's intentions."
- 
  
  Ransomware activity jumps 23% NCC Group has revealed that ransomware attacks surged 23% in October 2026 compared to September, with 1049 claimed incidents. The Gentlemen, N0n, Qilin, Akira, and Silent Ransom have claimed the most victims. Top targeted verticals included industrials, consumer discretionary, healthcare, IT, and consumer supplies. Check Point Research has reported a record 2,830 ransomware victims in Q3 2026, claimed by 117 ransomware brands, up from 91 in the previous quarter. Of these, 42 are new. "Ransom payments continued to diverge: average payments fell 45% quarter over quarter to just over $1 million, while the median rose 167% to $400,000," Check Point said. "The top 10 groups accounted for just 49% of victims, the first time groups outside the top ten collectively represented the majority." Qilin, The Gentlemen, and INC Ransom emerged as the most active groups during the period. Interestingly, while the top 10 groups accounted for 71% of victims in Q1 2026, the figure has declined to 58% in Q2 and only 49% in Q3, indicating a fragmentation of the threat landscape.
- 
  
  12,200 online stores compromised A new analysis from Guardio Labs has revealed that one online shop in 195 (i.e., about 12,200 of the 2.38 million stores) was hijacked in October 2026. The phenomenon has been codenamed CartJacked. "Three schemes go straight after shoppers: hand-offs to gambling and scam pages, fake 'I'm not a robot' checks that tell you to paste a command (about 900 shops), and card skimmers," Guardio said. "Of the ten commands the fake checks handed out, three still delivered malware, including a stealer for passwords and crypto wallets."
- 
  
  €26 million crypto trail uncovered A Europol-led operation along with authorities from 11 countries has disrupted 57 illegal IPTV services and the identification of 321 websites illegally offering copyrighted content as part of a five-day effort between November 16 and 20, 2026. The sites drew over 7.3 million visits each year. More than €26 million in cryptocurrency transactions have been traced so far. "The operation targeted a criminal market worth billions of euros annually, in which illegal streaming providers sell unauthorized access to premium television channels, live sports and films, often collecting subscription payments through cryptocurrency," Europol said. "The profits generated by these services do not simply disappear. They move through payment accounts, cryptocurrency wallets and intermediaries, making it harder for investigators to identify who is ultimately benefiting." No arrests have been announced.
- 
  
  10 million exposed NGINX services at risk Censys has revealed that more than 10 million exposed NGINX services are running an affected version with HTTP/2 that are vulnerable to a set of flaws called NGINX2Root that "could allow a remote, unauthenticated attacker to corrupt memory in an NGINX worker process when a set of specific features are enabled – leading to code execution where ASLR is disabled or the attacker can bypass it."
- 
  
  Power management software weaponized Broadcom-owned Symantec has disclosed details of an intrusion in which the attacker used CyberPower PowerPanel Business (PPB), a software that manages UPS devices, as a way to execute code on a domain controller, dump Active Directory secrets and launch a persistent implant. "PPB can run a script (a .cmd file in an extcmd folder) when a power-related event such as a voltage sag or outage is detected," Symantec said. "The attacker placed their own scripts in that folder through the product's web console and had the PowerPanel service, ppbed.exe, run them. The commands in this attack chain have ppbed.exe as their ancestor and run as SYSTEM. The attacker used this channel to download tools with certutil, then loaded a .NET assembly into memory using PowerShell, and ran ntdsutil and esentutl against the Active Directory database, ntds.dit." The same channel has also been used to launch an implant ("upnpcont.exe") that uses DLL sideloading to launch a suspicious DLL ("atl.dll"). "What this attack shows is that UPS, power-management, and other infrastructure software should be treated like any other potentially dual-use RMM product; used with network restrictions, unique credentials, vigilant patching, and process-level monitoring," Symantec said.
- 
  
  Banking middleware weaponized A new campaign called BankWeaver has targeted a Temenos Quantum Fabric deployment with an exposed authentication service that was configured to accept anonymous access to obtain administrator privileges and deliver malicious Java components via the platform's extension mechanism. The attack targeted an unspecified financial services institution in early September 2026. "Attackers could generate an anonymous token by accessing a public application and then exchange it for an administrator token on another exposed application," Forescout said. "The new token obtained by the attackers granted access to administrative functions within the Temenos Fabric platform, including managing running applications and creating new services." The malicious components delivered as part of the attack include: FabricShell, which provides arbitrary command execution and database queries, and FabricShadow, which collects host information, stages output locally, and exfiltrates results to remote servers. Temenos has since released updates and guidance to configure the service as private and advised customers to restrict internet access to Spotlight and Fabric administrative and authentication services.
- 
  
  Fake updates deliver Python backdoor A new wave of Microsoft Teams social engineering activity exhibiting similarities to Edgecution was uncovered by Arctic Wolf Labs last month. "In the October wave, following a lull in observed cases from August to September, new delivery artifacts and operational patterns were observed," the cybersecurity company said. "The campaign abuses a malicious Edge extension and Chrome Native Messaging to run a Python backdoor outside the browser sandbox. The activity shares early chain tradecraft with PREY-0059, including external-tenant Teams impersonation of IT support, legitimate runtimes paired with scripts, and S3-hosted payloads disguised as legitimate software. While PREY-0059 used S3 buckets named after targeted victims and delivered a Java-based RAT alongside a Java runtime, the current activity used generic Microsoft-themed tenants and buckets, an Edge extension, and a Python backdoor paired with a Python runtime."
One thing worth taking away from this week's stories is how much damage can happen without a particularly clever attack. A forgotten server, a stolen credential, or a feature nobody thought to monitor can be enough. AI may be changing how some attacks are carried out, but many of the ways attackers get in are still surprisingly ordinary.
The harder part is knowing what deserves attention before it becomes a problem. That includes software sitting quietly in the background, services exposed for convenience, and accounts with more access than they need. Somewhere between keeping things running and adding new capabilities, it's easy to lose track of what you've already put online. This week offers several good reasons to look again.

Side-by-side comparison testing

articles.title: Here are the best retro tech deals we've found for Black Friday — deals on retro tech for the modern PC setup
articles.text:
Here are the best retro tech deals we've found for Black Friday — deals on retro tech for the modern PC setup
Yesterday's tech, today.
The 1980s and 90s are now classed as "nostalgic," and the decades of neon, dayglow clothes made from synthetic fibers, and cereal with far too much sugar are now providing an escape from 21st-century life. These are the deals that bring back nostalgia, provide entertainment, and decorate your desk space with toys that your kids know nothing of. We've been scouring the internet to find the best deals on retro tech, selecting them based on our in-depth knowledge gained from years of gaming and hoarding old tech.
Retro gaming consoles, handhelds, and even replica arcade cabinets are on sale. Relive the glory years when your high score reigned supreme, and you could get a meal for $5 and still have change for the arcades!
- Mini Street Fighter 2 arcade cabinet for $59.99
- Xbox Duke controller (but smaller) for only $41.05
- 'IBM'-inspired mechanical keyboard under $74.99
Do you prefer gaming on your PC? Then we have retro-inspired gaming peripherals and keyboards, as well as mice for you. We also cover retro and nostalgic décor for your gaming setup, including a rather fabulous LEGO Game Boy and some genuinely "floppy" disks.
So let's dig into the deals!
Consoles and Handhelds
This bright yellow Atari 2600+ brings back memories of playing Pac-Man with my family at Christmas. Compatible with Atari 2600 and 7800 cartridges from back in the day and modern cartridges, this console comes with a double-feature cartridge that contains a new arcade-style version of Pac-Man and the original 2600 version. You also get one wireless Atari game controller. Additional controllers can be purchased in the colors of Pac-Man ghosts.
It looks like a retro computer, but this is really a 90s-inspired mini Bluetooth speaker with a smart pixel screen, an alarm clock, and focus tools. It looks like a retro computer, but this is really a 90s-inspired mini Bluetooth speaker with a smart pixel screen, an alarm clock, and focus tools. Play your tunes via Bluetooth, USB audio, or via TF card. The 1.77-inch screen can show pixel art, time, and more via a companion app. This is a tiny retro PC for those who want to show their love for a long-since-passed era.
I never owned a NeoGeo. Why? I was a teenager when they came out, and the games cost far too much for my pocket! This miniature recreation of a NeoGeo arcade cabinet sees 40 games (the average price of a Neo Geo game in the 1990s was $200, $8000 for all 40 games!) and includes the classics like Metal Slug, The King of Fighters and of course, Fatal Fury. The console has scaled versions of the original controls, a 3.5-inch screen, and runs on a USB-C power supply. Need a bigger screen? Connect via HDMI. External controllers, NeoGeo Mini Game controllers (available separately) can be used to retro game from the sofa!
Put M Bison, Vega, Ryu, and Chun-Li in your pocket and battle the world warriors as you commute to work! This handheld console comes with two versions of the popular brawler, Street Fighter II - Special Champion Edition and Super Street Fighter II. Super brings more fighters to the mix, offering new moves and strategies to bring down your opponents. This handheld unit features a 2.75-inch screen and a comfortable grip, so your dragon punch or yoga flame destroys your enemies.
With over 100 classic games in your pocket, your commute just became bearable. An officially licensed console, the Pocket Player Pro has classics such as Pong, Yars Revenge, Missile Command, and Breakout. You'll be swept away with classic gaming in the palm of your hand, with a high-resolution 2.75-inch screen and a headphone jack, which means you get all the glorious sounds of the golden age of gaming. My Arcade Pac-Man Pocket Player Pro is also available for $29.99.
What is this? A Nintendo Game Boy for ants? Joking aside, this GameBoy-styled console is tiny (0.7 x 0.3 x 1.2 inches!) and is powered by the Raspberry Pi Pico's RP2040 microcontroller. Programmable via a web interface, you can make your own games and demos to share with others. I've got one of these, and they are great fun to play with.
Arcade Cabinets
Zangief, Dhalsim, Chun-Li, Ryu. If these names just brought back a flood of memories, then this little cabinet is for you. Street Fighter 2 was a global phenomenon in the 1990s, and I played it for MANY hours on my SNES. This tiny, authentically recreated arcade cabinet features a 3.25-inch screen and scaled controls that mirror the original layout. The cabinet is only 6.9 x 5.6 x 8.7 inches in size, and it will look great on your desk. Buy a couple and link up with a friend to decide who is the world warrior
Controllers / Keyboards / Mice
The original Xbox came with "The Duke" controller, and unless you had huge hands, it was painful to play with. The "Duchess" is a smaller version of the famous controller, made for the Xbox Series X and your PC. The layout and aesthetic are so early 2000s, and I love it! Hall effect sticks, so no drift, a headphone jack, and bumpers that mimic the white and black buttons. All you need is Halo: Campaign Evolved, some Mountain Dew, and Cheetos, and you are back fragging newbs before class.
If you play retro games and more modern titles, then this is the controller for you. The overall shape is similar to the Super Nintendo, but it has the dual analog sticks and horns of a Sony PlayStation pad. This makes it useful for PlayStation emulation, SNES, and other 8/16-bit machines. But when you want to play newer titles, you won't need to reach for another pad, as this Xbox-designed pad will easily work on your PC! Best of all, this controller has Bluetooth, so you can game in comfort on your sofa!
This 87-key Bluetooth/2.4GHz/USB keyboard has all the retro vibes of a classic IBM-style keyboard, but without the huge price tag! You get a healthy dose of nostalgia in the aesthetics, but you get all the functionality that you need for a modern keyboard. Kailh Box Switch V2 White mechanical key switches, dye-sub PBT keycaps, and multiple connection options make this a great keyboard for retro computing and getting work done. The two large A and B "super" buttons can be programmed to do anything, probably to switch to Excel when the boss comes back into the office, saving you from a retro gaming dismissal.
An OG Xbox-inspired 87-key keyboard with RGB backlight! Translucent plastics were all the rage in the 1990s, and while the OG Xbox didn't have a translucent case until the Crystal, this keyboard is a homage to an era of carefree gaming! We get 87 keys with Kailh Jellyfish X switches, double-layered ABS keycaps, and a lovely translucent green plastic shell! The colored cursor keys are beautiful. Yes, we get the A and B super buttons that you can program to be any key, handy if you need to really make a point!
Looking like something that Syd Mead would have designed for Aliens or Blade Runner, this wireless rechargeable mouse has swappable buttons (it uses standard keycap stems) and can be used in wired, 2.4 GHz, and Bluetooth modes. It screams retro and would look great on your desk. The DPI is adjustable from 800-2400 in 200 DPI increments, so you could use it for gaming, but it'll probably be retro gaming with Doom, Dark Forces, or Sim City...right?
If the Nintendo NES were merged in some telepod / transporter accident with a wireless mouse, the 8-bit do N30 would be the result. You get a 2.4GHz wireless mouse in a NES-inspired case, and there is even a D-pad on the side. The mouse buttons are very similar to the NES controller, as is the case color. It may not be a Logitech MX Master 4, but it is fun!
Nostalgic Decoration
Build a 1990s PC without using a screwdriver! A construction kit for those of us old enough to remember doing this for real back in the 1990s! Build a desktop PC along with a CD-ROM drive, ISA / PCI cards, and a power supply, then crown the build with a monitor that has interchangeable screens and a keyboard/mouse combo. The PC measures 18.9 x 20 x 24 cm; it will look great on your shelf! Mac fans, you can pick up this Zuru building kit for under $10. I've got one, and it is really cute!

articles.title: Google a dû suspendre le chantier d’un data center en Belgique
articles.text:
La Région wallonne a ordonné l'arrêt du chantier d'un data center de Google près de Charleroi. Ses contrôleurs ont trouvé sur place un bâtiment de trois hectares presque terminé et construit sans permis valide, et l'administration va transmettre un procès-verbal au parquet.
La Wallonie fait de la résistance ! Le géant de Mountain View construit ce data center sur un ancien site minier d'une cinquantaine d'hectares, à cheval sur les communes de Farciennes, Aiseau-Presles et Sambreville. La Wallonie lui avait accordé un permis en 2024, avec des serveurs refroidis par air. Google a ensuite demandé à agrandir la surface construite et à refroidir ses machines avec l'eau de la Sambre, la tristement célèbre rivière qui longe le site. Après le recours d'un habitant, François Desquesnes (Les Engagés), ministre wallon de l'Aménagement du territoire, a refusé cette modification en août. Google a contesté ce refus devant le Conseil d'État, et il a continué à bâtir en attendant l'audience.
Google a construit un bâtiment de trois hectares sans permis
Greenpeace, qui soutient les opposants au projet, a alerté la Région. L'ONG a lancé une procédure d'urgence auprès du cabinet du ministre après avoir vu, sur des images prises au drone, que les travaux avaient beaucoup avancé en novembre. Le lendemain, des contrôleurs envoyés par la Région ont trouvé un bâtiment de 30 000 mètres carrés quasiment terminé et environ 300 ouvriers sur le chantier. « Nous avons donné l'ordre verbal d'arrêter les travaux », raconte Raphaël Stokis, fonctionnaire délégué de la Région wallonne, à la RTBF.
L'administration wallonne a confirmé cet ordre d'arrêt à l'AFP. « On a constaté une infraction majeure. Un procès-verbal va être adressé au parquet », prévient Nicolas Yernaux, porte-parole du Service public de Wallonie. Auprès de la RTBF, Google promet d'« entretenir un dialogue ouvert et collaboratif avec le gouvernement régional ».
Google et la Wallonie s'opposent surtout sur l'eau. Le géant américain demandait à pomper 600 mètres cubes par heure dans la Sambre et à rendre à la rivière moins d'un quart de ce volume. Pour refuser, François Desquesnes a mis en avant les ressources en eau limitées de la Wallonie et les sécheresses attendues ces prochaines années.
Google se heurte aussi aux autorités finlandaises, qui l'ont sommé de suspendre avant le 23 octobre deux chantiers de data centers, le temps d'évaluer leur impact sur l'environnement. Elles soupçonnent la société qui représente Google en Finlande d'avoir défriché plus de 300 hectares de forêt à Muhos sans l'évaluation obligatoire. En Belgique, le Conseil d'État examinera le recours de Google le 7 janvier, selon la RTBF.

articles.title: Tres alternativas para no ver películas en XUPER TV y no poner en peligro datos bancarios
articles.text:
Utilizar Xuper TV es un grave error porque la aplicación distribuye contenidos sin autorización y puede dejar expuestos los datos personales, bancarios y el funcionamiento del dispositivo.
Su instalación suele requerir archivos APK descargados fuera de las tiendas oficiales, un mecanismo que aumenta el riesgo de incorporar malware, programas espía o accesos no autorizados.
Además, las plataformas de este tipo pueden ser bloqueadas sin aviso y presentan una oferta inestable, con anuncios invasivos o intentos de fraude. Frente a esa situación, hay servicios gratuitos y legales que permiten acceder a películas, series y canales sin recurrir a aplicaciones de origen desconocido.
Qué tres alternativas gratuitas y seguras a Xuper TV existen
Pluto TV dispone de canales en vivo, películas, series y programas a demanda financiados con publicidad. No requiere una suscripción paga y, en gran parte de su catálogo, tampoco exige crear una cuenta. Su programación varía según el país, pero ha incluido títulos como CSI Miami, The Walking Dead, Daredevil y Naruto.
Otra opción es RTVE Play, la plataforma de Radio Televisión Española. Su catálogo reúne series, películas, documentales, informativos y producciones de la televisión pública, entre ellas contenidos vinculados con MasterChef. Algunas emisiones pueden tener restricciones fuera de España por los derechos de transmisión.
La tercera alternativa es Plex, un servicio que ofrece películas, series y canales gratuitos con anuncios. Permite organizar y reproducir una biblioteca propia de archivos audiovisuales legales. Su programación ha incluido producciones como Medici, The Dick Van Dyke Show y Hot Ones, aunque los títulos disponibles cambian según el territorio.
Las tres aplicaciones se pueden obtener desde las tiendas oficiales, una diferencia central frente a Xuper TV. Antes de descargar cualquier plataforma, conviene revisar el desarrollador, los permisos solicitados y las condiciones de uso.
Por qué es inseguro usar Xuper TV
La principal alerta está en el método de instalación. Xuper TV no suele descargarse desde canales oficiales, sino mediante archivos APK obtenidos en sitios externos. Esos paquetes no siempre pasan controles de seguridad y pueden contener software diseñado para recopilar contraseñas, información bancaria u otros datos del usuario.
Asimismo, existe un riesgo legal. La aplicación ofrece películas, series y señales pagas sin contar con los permisos correspondientes de los titulares de derechos. Por esa razón, servicios y fabricantes de dispositivos han reforzado las medidas para impedir su uso.
Este tipo de aplicaciones puede incluir virus, spyware y herramientas para acceder a información personal. La recomendación es evitar descargas externas y elegir servicios con presencia en tiendas verificadas.
Fire TV eliminó Xuper TV de su biblioteca de aplicaciones
Amazon retiró Xuper TV, antes llamada Magis TV, de la biblioteca de Fire TV como parte de sus controles contra aplicaciones que distribuyen contenido protegido sin autorización.
La empresa reforzó la detección de servicios incluidos en listados de la Alliance for Creativity and Entertainment (ACE), una organización que combate la piratería audiovisual.
Cuando el sistema identifica una aplicación bloqueada, muestra una advertencia e inhabilita su funcionamiento. La medida también alcanza a servicios instalados de forma manual mediante APK.
Qué nuevo modelo de Fire TV hay
El modelo más reciente de la línea es el Fire TV Stick 4K de tercera generación, presentado por Amazon en septiembre de 2026.
El dispositivo reproduce contenido en resolución 4K y es compatible con HDR10, HDR10+, HLG y Wi‑Fi 6. Incluye 8 GB de almacenamiento, un procesador de cuatro núcleos a 1,7 GHz y Bluetooth 5.3.
El equipo estrena el sistema operativo Vega OS 2.0 y una carcasa más delgada. También puede alimentarse desde el puerto USB del televisor mediante la función Direct Power, por lo que reduce la necesidad de cables adicionales.
Amazon incorporó un nuevo control remoto con botones de mayor relieve y acceso a Alexa+. El modelo está disponible en mercados seleccionados, mientras que la empresa mantiene otras versiones, como Fire TV Stick HD y Fire TV Stick 4K Max.

Linux Mint 27 está a caminho e estas são as novidades
Distribuição Linux Mint 27 "Adrien" beta já está disponível, trazendo suporte prolongado (LTS) até 2031 e kernel 7.0.
Você já pode testar a nova versão de uma das distribuições Linux mais amigáveis da atualidade: o pacote beta do Linux Mint 27 “Adrien” foi liberado para download. A novidade tem o ambiente de desktop Cinnamon 6.8 com suporte completo ao Wayland como destaque, mas há mais atributos interessantes.
Antes de irmos ao que há de novo, convém deixar claro que esta é uma versão com suporte prolongado (LTS) e que, por isso, receberá atualizações pelo menos até 2031. Vale destacar também que a novidade é baseada no Ubuntu 26.04 LTS e vem com o kernel Linux 7.0.
O Cinnamon 6.8 foi introduzido neste mês de novembro e se destaca por trazer aprimoramentos nos gestos de touchpad e de tela sensível ao toque, além de avanços no gerenciamento de conexões de rede, tudo isso sem abrir mão de sua interface leve e intuitiva.
Outro avanço notável é que, nesta versão, o ambiente de desktop passa a ter suporte completo ao Wayland, o moderno servidor gráfico que vem substituindo o tradicional X11 em diversas distribuições, como Ubuntu e Fedora.
Note, porém, que o X11 ainda é padrão no Linux Mint 27 beta. O Wayland deve ser ativado pelo usuário.
O Linux Mint 27 beta também traz novos aplicativos nativos como parte do projeto XApps, que visa disponibilizar ferramentas que funcionem independentemente do ambiente gráfico escolhido pelo usuário. Os destaques são estes:
- Clockenstein: app de calendário, suportando tanto agendas locais quanto integração com o Google Calendar e serviços compatíveis com CalDAV;
- Superlight: monitora o sistema para exibir o status de recursos como CPU, GPU, memória RAM, temperaturas, rede e armazenamento;
- Velocitty: é uma ferramenta de terminal com suporte a múltiplas abas, paletas de cores, SSH e execução automática de comandos na inicialização;
- Unfold: é um gerenciador de arquivos compactados leve e compatível com vários formatos, como RAR;
- Xepub: permite ler e-books no formato EPUB, suportando recursos como marcações, anotações e tradução de palavras.
O Linux Mint está há algum tempo com o recurso de hibernação desativado por padrão. Isso porque essa funcionalidade foi desabilitada no Ubuntu, distribuição que é a base do projeto, vale relembrar. A boa notícia é que a versão 27 marca o retorno da opção de hibernar.
Vale deixar claro que a hibernação é diferente da suspensão, pois salva a sessão em uma área do SSD / HD e desliga o computador. Já a suspensão faz a máquina entrar em baixo consumo de energia, mas sob o risco de a carga de bateria acabar se esse modo for mantido por muito tempo.
Mas os próprios desenvolvedores do Linux Mint alertam que o retorno do computador da hibernação pode ser lento e que esse modo exige uma boa quantidade de espaço livre de armazenamento (swap) para funcionar.
Há vários outros atributos no Linux Mint 27, entre eles:
- Nemo: o gerenciador de arquivos agora conta com um painel que permite ao usuário conferir o conteúdo de áudios, imagens e vídeos sem precisar abri-los;
- Screenshot: a ferramenta de captura de tela foi reescrita, permitindo registrar janelas com ou sem sombras, por exemplo;
- Papéis de parede: agora é possível definir um wallpaper diferente para cada monitor;
- Notificações: o usuário pode ativar ou desativar notificações individualmente para cada aplicativo.
Você pode baixar a imagem ISO do Linux Mint 27 “Adrien” em um dos links da página de anúncio da versão beta. Depois, use uma ferramenta como o Rufus para criar um pendrive de instalação ou de teste (modo “live”).
Ali, você pode escolher versões com o ambiente Cinnamon retratado aqui, com Xfce ou com MATE.
O site OMG! Ubuntu faz um alerta importante: a distribuição conta com um novo instalador que não oferece configuração simplificada de dual boot com Windows ou outra distribuição. Para isso, é necessário fazer particionamento manual.
Leve em consideração também que estamos falando de uma versão beta, que está mais sujeita a falhas ou instabilidades, portanto. Nesse sentido, a dica é baixá-la somente para testes, não para usá-la como sistema principal.
O lançamento da versão estável do Linux Mint 27 é esperado para o fim de 2026 ou início de 2027.

articles.title: Get a staggering $1,400 off an RTX 5070-powered HP Omen 35L gaming desktop sporting an Intel Core Ultra 7 CPU and 32GB of DDR5 — at 38% discount, this performant mid-tower prebuilt PC packs a punch
articles.text:
Get a staggering $1,400 off an RTX 5070-powered HP Omen 35L gaming desktop sporting an Intel Core Ultra 7 CPU and 32GB of DDR5 — at 38% discount, this performant mid-tower prebuilt PC packs a punch
HP's Omen 35L prebuilt PC comes in at $2199.
HP's Omen prebuilt PC comes in a standard mid-tower size, but crams in an RTX 5070 GPU, 32GB of DDR5-6000 memory, and an Intel Core Ultra 7 265F. Boasting a steep 38% discount at HP for Black Friday, this system offers mid-range specs at a comfortable mid-range price. One thing to note about HP's modern prebuilt desktops is that, unlike the days of yore, they actually use standardized parts, meaning that upgrading the system later down the line (perhaps when PC component pricing calms down), you'll be all set to upgrade without the hassle of having to work around proprietary boards and parts.
Alongside the CPU GPU, and RAM, you also get a 1TB PCIe Gen 4 drive for all of the games you'll download onto the system, and there's also a spare slot, in case you want to expand the capacity in the future, and whenever the price of RAM comes down, you might also wish to populate the two empty DIMM slots over on the motherboard.
Get an RTX 5070-powered PC, paired with an Intel Core Ultra 7 265F, 32GB of Kingston Fury DDR5-6000 RAM, and a 1TB SSD; the system also offers plenty of space to upgrade storage and memory capacities in the future. Expect a solid mid-tower chassis with an 850W power supply and an Intel B860 chipset motherboard.
Intel has not specified the make or manufacturer of the B860 motherboard contained within the system, but we do get further details about its I/O and connectivity options. Expect a Realtek connectivity chipset with support for WI-Fi 6 and Bluetooth 5.3 for all your controllers and peripherals, alongside a host of ports, including 2x USB-C 10Gbps, 4x USB-A ports at 5Gbps, and a further 4x USB-A 2.0 ports.
The entire system makes for a solid 1440p-focused build, and with the RTX 5070 paired nicely with Intel's Core Ultra 7 265KF, the 20-core CPU, consisting of 8 P-cores and 12 E-cores, will perform nicely, with boost clocks at up to 5.4GHz on the P-cores. Therefore, our mystery unspecified motherboard will be running LGA 1851, which is running towards its end of life. So, while other aspects of the system remain fairly upgradable, do be aware that if you want a CPU upgrade, drop-in options will be limited without having to switch platforms to Nova Lake or other future architectures. Despite this, you can't refute a good offer, and armed with a staggering $1400 off its current MSRP at HP for Black Friday, it still offers heaps of value in the current climate.

articles.title: Le Sénat supprime la hausse de TVA sur les abonnements Canal+
articles.text:
Le Sénat a maintenu à 10 % la TVA de votre abonnement Canal+ dans le budget 2027. Jeudi 26 novembre, les sénateurs ont supprimé, contre l'avis du gouvernement, l'article qui alignait la télévision payante sur les 20 % de Netflix, Disney+ ou Prime Video.
Il n'y a pas de petites économies. Le gouvernement de Sébastien Lecornu voulait mettre fin au taux réduit des offres de télévision en direct, et Canal+ était le premier touché. Les députés avaient supprimé cette hausse le 2 novembre, par 45 voix contre 15. Mais deux jours plus tard, ils ont rejeté toute la partie recettes du budget, et le Sénat a reçu le texte initial du Gouvernement, avec la hausse de TVA. Les deux chambres du Parlement ont donc refusé la mesure, mais le Gouvernement la défend toujours.
Les sénateurs refusent de taxer Canal+ à 20 %
Christine Lavarde, sénatrice LR et rapporteure générale du budget, avait fait adopter la suppression de l'article 16 en commission des finances le 12 novembre, selon CB News. En séance publique, les sénateurs l'ont suivie. Pour eux, la hausse « affecterait principalement le groupe Canal+, qui estime son incidence sur son chiffre d'affaires à environ 200 millions d'euros par an », un montant confirmé par les chiffres de l'administration, rapporte BFM Business.
Les sénateurs rappellent aussi que l'administration et les chaînes concernées ont mis plusieurs années à s'entendre sur la TVA des bouquets qui mélangent chaînes en direct et vidéo à la demande. L'administration fiscale a fixé ces règles en septembre 2025, et Canal+ a réglé trois mois plus tard son litige avec le fisc en acceptant de verser 363 millions d'euros. Le fisc avait d'abord proposé un redressement de 655 millions d'euros.
Ils défendent enfin le cinéma et le sport. Canal+ finance ces deux secteurs et avait menacé de réduire ses contributions si la TVA doublait. La fin du taux réduit aurait des « conséquences majeures sur le financement du sport et du cinéma », préviennent-ils. En juillet, le groupe avait signé avec les organisations du cinéma un accord de 980 millions d'euros sur cinq ans, à partir de 2028.
Selon l'amendement des députés, la hausse de TVA rapporterait 304 millions d'euros à l'État dès 2027. Devant eux, David Amiel, ministre de l'Action et des Comptes publics, avait défendu « un article à 400 millions d'euros ».
Le prix de votre abonnement Canal+ dépend du vote final du budget
Souvenez-vous, début octobre, Maxime Saada, président du directoire de Canal+, avait réagi au projet du gouvernement sur RTL. Il avait parlé d'une décision « politique » et « anti-économique », puis annoncé une hausse de l'ordre de 10 % des abonnements si la TVA passait à 20 %. Selon lui, elle interviendrait « pas avant 2028-2029 », car Canal+ doit attendre la fin de vos périodes d'engagement.
Le vote des sénateurs ne règle pas la question. Ils doivent voter sur toute la partie recettes ce week-end, puis sur l'ensemble du budget le 9 décembre, selon Echos du Net. Députés et sénateurs chercheront ensuite une version commune. Matignon renvoie à décembre un compromis entre sa copie et celle du Sénat, selon l'AFP. Jusqu'à l'adoption définitive du budget, vous payez 10 % de TVA sur votre abonnement.
Si le gouvernement obtient gain de cause, la hausse réelle serait un peu inférieure à 10 %. À prix hors taxes inchangé, le prix TTC augmenterait de 9,09 %. Vous paieriez ainsi l'abonnement Canal+ 27,26 euros par mois au lieu de 24,99 euros, d'après le calcul du comparateur Selectra. Sur une box, seule la part télévision du forfait est taxée à 10 %, et la hausse serait donc plus faible sur votre facture.

articles.title: Tons of motherboards are on sale right now, some over 40% off – we sorted through them for you and picked out a few of the best deals
articles.text:
Tons of motherboards are on sale right now, some over 40% off – we sorted through them for you and picked out a few of the best deals
Find the best of the best Black Friday motherboard deals from around the web
During the ongoing Black Friday deals this week, a lot of motherboards have gone on sale, which has kept the experts at Tom’s Hardware quite busy finding deals for you and updating our best motherboard deals article over the last few days. We’ve seen boards from AMD and Intel from the latest platforms and even a generation or two back since everything, including RAM, video cards, and storage, remains pricey. We’ve seen deals on AM4-based boards using the less expensive but still capable DDR4, and plenty of deals on Intel motherboards, too. In short, there’s something for everyone on sale right now.
It can be difficult to sort through all of the options, so we’ve picked out a few of the best deals while still keeping other considerations in mind. While it’s nice to pay less, a deal doesn’t really benefit you if you don’t have the functionality you need. It’s still critical to understand your wants and needs prior to buying and making sure you have everything you need before clicking the ‘buy’ button.
Gigabyte's Z890 Aorus Master, which we covered back in 2024, is a great all-around motherboard for Intel's Arrow Lake and Arrow Lake refresh chips. Not only does it look good, with full coverage of M.2 sockets and the signature Gigabyte Aorus design elements, but it also brings the latest hardware for the platform.
It offers fast networking with 10 GbE and integrated Wi-Fi 7 (320 MHz), ample storage with five M.2 sockets (2x PCIe 5.0) and four SATA ports, loads of USB ports (14) on the rear I/O including 40 Gbps Thunderbolt 4, a premium audio solution with a last-gen flagship-class Realtek ALC1220 codec and ESS DAC chip, and fast memory support, up to DDR5-9500+ (OC). And we can't forget the EZ features, either. At almost half the original MSRP, this is one of the best deals on a premium Intel motherboard.
The Gigabyte Z890 Aorus Master (we reviewed) delivers Arrow Lake support, Wi-Fi 7, Thunderbolt 4, five M.2 slots (2x PCIe 5.0), 10GbE LAN, fast RAM support to DDR5-9500+ (OC), and 14 USB ports in a cleaner ATX design. It also uses a high-end audio solution with integrated DAC.
Next up is another Intel LGA1851 socket board, this time from the budget-class B860 chipset in Gigabyte's B860 Aorus Elite Wi-Fi 7 Ice. This icy-white, low-priced motherboard offers a cheaper entry point to the latest Intel platform. While the discount isn't the highest we've seen, its appearance and comprehensive specs make it one of the best all-around deals for an inexpensive B860 motherboard.
Aside from the white PCH and heatsinks, the Aorus Elite Wi-Fi 7 Ice has three full-length PCIe slots and heatsinks covering all three M.2 sockets (1x PCIe 5.0). It offers four SATA ports for legacy storage and a basic audio solution. Networking consists of 2.5 GbE and Wi-Fi 7 (160 MHz). It also has plenty of USB ports on the rear I/O, including one USB4. If you're looking for a white motherboard for your shiny new Intel processor that won't break the bank, check this one out before the deal expires.
Save on this Icy white Gigabyte B860 Aorus Elite Wifi 7 Ice motherboard and jump into the latest intel platform for less. The board comes with three M.2 sockets, three full length PCIe slots, fast Wi-Fi 7 and 2.5 GbE, as well as Gigabyte's EZ features.
The next deal is a mid-range AM5 motherboard: the X870E Aorus Elite Wi-Fi 7. This motherboard supports AM5-based processors from the Ryzen 7000/8000/9000 series, including the X3D chips. The Aorus Elite offers another well-rounded solution with comprehensive specifications and a look that's sure to stand out inside your chassis.
Hardware-wise, you get all of the fixings, including four M.2 sockets (a whopping 3x PCIe 5.0), four SATA ports for storage, a flagship-class last-gen Realtek ALC1220 audio codec (no amps/DACs), 2.5 GbE and integrated Wi-Fi 7 (160 MHz), three full-length PCIe slots for expansion, and plenty of USB ports on the rear I/O, including two USB4 (40 Gbps) Type-C ports. And don't forget about the EZ DIY features.
Gigabyte's X870E Aorus Elite Wifi 7 offers fast Wi-Fi 7 and networking, ample USB ports including dual USB4 (40 Gbps) ports, four M.2 sockets and four SATA ports for storage, and a slew of EZ DIY features on top of a black aesthetic. It's a great base for any AM5 processor.
Next is an awesome deal from Woot.com for a budget-class AM5 board, MSI's B850 Tomahawk Max Wi-Fi, which we reviewed back in 2025 and gave four stars. For the money, the Tomahawk Max offers some mid-range class features, including 5 GbE and integrated Wi-Fi 7 (320 MHz), ample USB ports on the rear I/O, including three Type-C (though the only 20 Gbps-plus is on the front). It's also one of the only boards at this price point with two PCIe 5.0 M.2 sockets (total of four).
Other features include three full-length PCIe slots for expansion, Supplemental PCIe power, and MSI's EZ DIY features like EZ M.2 Shield Frozr II and EZ M.2 Clip II to make M.2 installation seamless. This also extends to the GPU, where a simple button locks/unlocks the graphics card. For the current sale price, there isn't a better B850 board around.
Save big in this budget B850 motherboard from MSI. The Tomahawk MAx Wifi is an update from teh original offering Wi-Fi 7 and 5 GbE, ample USB ports, four M.2 sockets (dual PCIe 5.0) and more.
