Black Week: Galaxy S26 FE cai ainda mais e chega a 47% OFF com cupom
Galaxy S26 FE (128 GB) com tela AMOLED e câmera de 50 MP atinge o menor preço desde o lançamento, com desconto de 47% no Pix com cupom exclusivo no app Magalu
O Galaxy S26 FE de 128 GB está saindo por R$ 2.899 no Pix com cupom INFLU300 apenas pelo app do Magazine Luiza. O premium acessível da Samsung, com tela de 120 Hz e melhorias de IA, atinge o menor preço desde o lançamento na Black Week 2026, com desconto de 47% sobre o original de R$ 5.499.
O menor preço que já encontramos para o Galaxy S26 FE 5G 128 GB foi R$ 2.899, na Black Friday de 2026 (Magalu). Fora de datas promocionais, o melhor foi R$ 3.249,10 (Magalu, 5/11/2026).
O novo Galaxy S26 FE possui uma tela LTPO AMOLED Dinâmico 2X de 6,7″, com taxa de 120 Hz e brilho de 1.900 nits. Essa combinação reproduz cores vibrantes com alta fluidez, além de entregar garantia de visibilidade em qualquer situação.
Seu chip Exynos 2500 de 3 nanômetros e os 8 GB de RAM sustentam apps pesados e novas funções de IA, como a assistente Bixby melhorada, que lê infos no celular, e o recurso My FanCam, que acompanha a pessoa durante filmagens.
O kit principal de câmeras filma em 8K. Ele inclui wide de 50 MP com OIS e ultrawide de 12 MP, que captam belas cenas ao ar livre, e telefoto de 8 MP com zoom óptico de 3x para aproximações. A frontal de 12 MP tira ótimas selfies e filma em 4K a 60 fps.
O corpo de alumínio do S26 FE é revestido de ambos os lados pelo vidro Gorilla Glass Victus+, resistente contra pancadas e quedas. A certificação IP68 confere proteção em cenários como poeira intensa e mergulhos acidentais.
Sua bateria de 4.900 mAh tem autonomia de até 29 horas de reprodução de vídeo, segundo a Samsung. O suporte ao carregamento rápido de 45 W via USB-C e de 15 W sem fio garante energia para um dia inteiro com apenas alguns minutos na tomada.
O Galaxy S26 FE de 128 GB (R$ 2.899 no Pix com cupom INFLU300 apenas pelo app Magalu) será atualizado até o Android 24 e possui conectividade 5G, Wi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth 5.4 e NFC.
A edição 2026 da Black Friday é amanhã (27), e lojas como Magalu se preparam para oferecer diversas ofertas em eletrônicos com cupons e condições especiais até a Cyber Monday, na próxima segunda-feira (30).
Acompanhe o Achados no Telegram ou WhatsApp e não perca nenhuma promoção.
Aviso de ética: ao clicar em um link de afiliado, o preço não muda para você e recebemos uma comissão.

articles.title: I review fitness trackers for a living: I’ve found 18 discreet screenless wearables deals for Black Friday on Garmin, Fitbit, Oura, Whoop and more
articles.text:
Don’t want a smartwatch? 18 deals on discreet screenless fitness trackers from Whoop, Garmin, Fitbit, Oura and many more, picked by a wearable-tech expert
Today's best deals on screenless smart wear
The Black Friday deals are here, and as TechRadar's Senior Fitness & Wearables Editor, I've been looking primarily at the discounts on wearable health tech.
The big trending category this year was screenless — from bands like the Whoop, Fitbit Air and Garmin Cirqa, to smart rings such as the Oura Ring 5. If you're looking to track your workouts, sleep and recovery without another screen on your wrist, then these deals are for you.
• Browse all today's best Black Friday deals in the UK
• Browse all today's best Black Friday deals in the US
On this page you'll find Black Friday deals on a range of fitness trackers for all kinds of budgets, with offers in both the US and UK. Some have a mandatory subscription attached (and are clearly marked) while others are subscription-free.
For US shoppers, I've picked deals such as the Oura Ring 5 in Silver or Black from $299 (was $399) at Walmart, or a 12-month membership for Whoop Peak at $199.99 (was $239.99) from Amazon.
In the UK, I've spotted a deal on the trending Google Fitbit Air, which is down to £74.99 (was £84.99) at Amazon, and even the Garmin Cirqa (was £179.99 now £169.99 at H.Samuel), along with bigger discounts on devices like the Oura and Samsung Galaxy Rings
I've also included an extensive list of other US and UK deals below, and I'll be keeping this page updated today and over the weekend.
US Quick Deals

- Whoop Peak 12-month membership: was $239.99 now $199.99 at Amazon

UK Quick Deals

Today's best screenless fitness tracker deals in the US
We rated this subscription-free Oura alternative 4/5 stars in our review, with our tester noting "its huge battery life (up to 12 days) and sleep apnea tracking". With over $90 off and no extra fees, this deal undercuts Oura by a large margin.

Whoop's annual membership program is divided into three tiers: Whoop One (now $189.99, was $199.99), with the fewest features, Whoop Peak (now $199.99, saving $239.99), with extras, and Whoop Life (now $299.99, was $359.99) , which comes with the expensive MG tracker with extra heart health features. 
In my opinion, most people are overpaying for the MG even with the discounts, so if you want Whoop I'd pay $10 more than the lowest tier and grab the Whoop Peak at $40 off. Bear in mind that this is an annual subscription. 
Read moreRead less▼
Polar's Loop fitness tracker, like Whoop, is a screenless fitness tracking puck covered by a sweat-wicking fabric band, for continuous heart rate monitoring, with metrics accessible via the app. Unlike Whoop, which is based on a membership, there's no subscription fee — although the app isn't as good.

Somehow 40% slimmer than the prior generation, the Oura Ring 5 is seeing a $100 discount at Walmart right now, bringing the premium finishes down to $399. It's a phenomenal health-tracking platform with all kinds of insights — but there is a $5.99 monthly fee.

The cheaper Silver and Black finishes get the same $100 discount as their pricier siblings. All the same sensor arrays and technology are present and correct in these tiny trackers — the only difference is the finish.

The still-excellent Oura Ring 4 is down to under $250 right now, and offers five-to-eight days of battery life, and impressive health and sleep tracking. It's the cheapest way to get a new Oura Ring for Black Friday.

Prices vary on the gorgeous Oura Ring 4 Ceramic range depending on the popularity of color, but the cheapest by far is this Midnight option, at just $279.

The Samsung Galaxy Ring is subscription-free, so if you did choose to get it instead of the Oura (provided you use the Samsung Health app, which isn't really compatible with iPhones) you'd save yourself even more later down the line.

Whoop's cheapest annual membership programme, Whoop One, hasn't been discounted at all at £169. For an extra £20, you get plenty of extra features including the Whoop Age score, without overpaying for Whoop Life at an extra £100 a year. Bear in mind this is an annual subscription.

While there aren't many discounts on the Fitbit Air, I did spot this £10-off deal on the Performance Loop model. It makes a great-value fitness tracker even better, especially as the Air was only released recently.

While that's not a huge saving, I do love the Cirqa — it's my favourite screenless tracker over Whoop, the Polar Loop and the Fitbit Air, and the optional Garmin Connect+ subscription isn't essential in order to use and enjoy it.

A small but significant £15 discount on the Amazfit Helio Strap, another Whoop alternative we rated highly in our Amazfit Helio Strap review. It's great for post-workout recovery, sleep tracking and all-day wear.

Save £100 (25%) on the Oura Ring 5 in Silver or Black in all sizes, and enjoy seven-day battery life and sleep tracking. This offer gets you the same sensor array and features as above, but in a more premium finish, with £100 off the more expensive Brushed Silver, Gold, Deep Rose and Stealth colours.

The Oura Ring 4's price has been lowered across the board in the UK to reflect that it's no longer the latest tech, but you can still save a bit more on premium finishes like this beautiful pastel Ceramic Cloud model, dependent on stocks of the different sizes.

Another subscription-free Oura alternative from biohacking company Ultrahuman. You can track sleep, stress, HRV, workouts and more with its comprehensive app.

The subscription-free Oura alternative with a big battery life, sleep apnea and activity tracking is almost £100 off at Amazon right now. The ring goes from middle-of-the-pack in terms of value to top of the leaderboard at under £170 all-in.

articles.title: The absolute best Black Friday deals we’ve found (so far)
articles.text:
This year’s Black Friday deals have launched in waves over the past several weeks, but now the floodgates have officially opened. You can now take advantage of the lowest prices we’ve seen in-store and online for video games, wireless earbuds, TVs, e-readers, robot vacuums, and so much more. We can’t guarantee a deal you’ve had your eye on will last through Cyber Monday; however, if prior years are any indication, most will stick around through the long holiday weekend.
The absolute best Black Friday deals we’ve found (so far)
Many of our favorite gadgets and gizmos are cheaper than they’ve been all year, making now the perfect time to shop.
As usual, we sorted through thousands of deals to find the ones truly worth sharing, with an eye for the products and services we’ve tested here at The Verge. With prices up across multiple categories due to RAMageddon, some deals may not seem as big as in prior years. For example, Apple’s latest MacBook Air recently fell to its pre-price-hike level for the first time since July. That’s a deal to us, and several other discounts are taking a similar shape. We’ll provide context when possible and keep this post updated throughout the day.
AirPods Pro 3
Apple’s AirPods Pro 3 deliver the best noise cancellation and sound quality of any AirPods yet, along with a more comfortable, secure fit and improved water resistance. They also feature built-in heart rate tracking for workouts and support live translations for a handful of languages. Read our review.
Disney Plus, Hulu Bundle
You can get an ad-supported Disney Plus and Hulu bundle for $4.99 a month ($8 off) for an entire year. Both streaming services feature a deep catalog of new and classic TV shows and movies, including The Simpsons, Andor, Toy Story 5, and The Fantastic Four: First Steps.
Anker Universal Charger (100W)
Anker’s durable travel adapter delivers up to 100W of power and works in over 200 countries. It doesn’t support AC plugs, but it does offer a trio of USB-C ports and a nifty LCD display to keep tabs on the charge percentage.
Xteink X4 Classic pocket e-reader
With a 4.3-inch E Ink screen, the Xteink X4 is smaller and more pocketable than any Kindle and Kobo model currently available. It has some drawbacks — it’s limited to TXT and EPUB files — but it’s great for tinkering; it also has a magnetic mount so you can stick it to the back of MagSafe-ready phones.
Nintendo Switch 2 + Mario Kart World Bundle
The Nintendo Switch 2 features a 7.9-inch LCD display, magnetically attached Joy-Con 2 controllers, backward compatibility with most original Switch games, and exclusive titles like Donkey Kong Bananza and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Read our review.
HBO Max
An HBO Max Basic subscription provides access to shows like A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, The Last of Us, and The Pitt, as well as films like Superman and Weapons. You can get a year of the monthly ad-supported subscription for $5.49 a month (about $6 off) until December 1st.
Eufy Omni C28
The Eufy Omni C28 combines excellent mopping performance with a small self-cleaning dock that’s well suited for apartments and other smaller spaces. It navigates around furniture and into tight areas with ease, while its roller mop does a great job cleaning hard floors.
SwitchBot Bot Rechargeable
Do you ever wish you could turn on your coffee maker or hit the light switch without getting up? The SwitchBot Bot lets you do that. All you need to do is stick the inexpensive contraption on a standard button or rocker switch, which will allow you to control or schedule your pet feeder, garage door, and a wide range of other devices from your smartphone.
Apple AirTag (second-gen)
Apple’s latest AirTags feature an upgraded ultra-wideband chip for more precise location tracking, a noticeably louder speaker, and an expanded Bluetooth range. Read our review.
Kodak Charmera Keychain Digital Camera
The Chamera is not a good camera, but that’s not the point. Kodak’s charming, keychain-friendly tchotchke lets you snap lo-fi memories on a whim, with an ultra-small 1.6-megapixel sensor, a built-in LED flash, and the tiniest amount of storage.
LIFX Everyday Smart Light Bulbs (two-pack)
LIFX’s dimmable, color-changing bulbs offer Wi-Fi connectivity, simple setup, and Matter compatibility, so they work with any major smart home platform. The company is currently trialing a Thread beta that will bring the option to add Thread connectivity to all its Matter devices.
Apple MacBook Air (M5)
Apple’s latest MacBook Air features an M5 chip and starts with 512GB of storage, with significantly faster performance than prior generations. It’s still an excellent machine despite the higher base price, especially given the battery life and speakers. Read our review.
Octobuddy Classic
Who needs magnets when you have suction cups? Octobuddy’s cheap silicone mount works with most phones to provide hands-free flexibility whenever necessary. It features 24 single-sided cups, which allow you to stick your phone to a mirror, window, or any other surface you think will provide that perfect TikTok angle.
Peacock
Peacock is a great way to catch up on a wealth of content from NBC’s various networks, whether you plan to rewatch The Office or catch up on all things Bravo. A Premium subscription also grants access to films from studios like Universal Pictures and DreamWorks, along with live sports and a host of Peacock Originals.
Samsung P9 microSD Express card
The P9 is great if you need more storage for your Nintendo Switch 2. The microSD Express card offers sequential read speeds of up to 800MB/s, but only gadgets with a microSD Express card slot can take full advantage of the highest speeds. That includes certain cameras, tablets, and drones with a microSD USH-I slot.
Fanttik X9 Pro Portable Tire Inflator
The Fanttik X9 Pro can inflate a car tire in under a minute, making routine maintenance fast and easy. There are four one-click presets for cars, motorcycles, bikes, and balls, along with a manual mode that reaches a maximum pressure of 150PSI.
Apple iPad (11th generation)
Apple’s 11th-gen iPad follows up the 10th-gen model with a new A16 chip and few other changes — and is the only Apple tablet to not support Apple Intelligence.
Anker 140W 2-in-1 USB-C to USB-C Cable
No one should have to deal with a rat’s nest behind their desk when devices like Anker’s 2-in-1 USB-C cable exist. The handy USB-C cable splits at the end, giving you the ability to charge up to two devices from a single port. That means you can split power between a phone and tablet or juice a 16-inch MacBook Pro to 50 percent in just 20 minutes using a single port.
Wuben G5 rechargeable flashlight
The Wuben G5 flashlight is as small as a Zippo lighter, yet far more versatile, with a bright, rotatable light that can shine in numerous colors. It features USB-C charging and has an adjustable clip.
Sony WH-1000XM4C
Sony’s XM4 noise-canceling headphones were so good, the company brought them back with a few minor improvements. They still offer great ANC, a timeless foldable design, and delivering performance nearly on par with Sony’s newer flagships at a fraction of the cost.
Govee Table Lamp 2
Govee’s Table Lamp 2 is way more fun than your average table lamp. The color-changing device boasts built-in scheduling and more than 60 dynamic lighting effects, including preset scenes for various holidays. You can even create custom color combos for when “Dandelion” and other presets just aren’t cutting it.
Kindle Paperwhite (2024)
Compared to the last-gen base Kindle model (currently $119.99), the Paperwhite is a much better value. It features waterproofing, better battery life, faster page-turning speeds, and a higher-pixel-density screen that’s slightly larger (7 inches vs. 6 inches).
Sonos Play
The water-resistant Sonos Play sits between the Roam 2 and Move 2, offering a balance of portability and room-filling sound. It delivers up to 24 hours of battery life, with a built-in loop for easy carrying. You can also use it as a power bank and pair it with other Sonos speakers over Bluetooth when Wi-Fi isn’t available. Read our review.
Zepath USB-C Li-ion AA Batteries
Rechargeable AA batteries are handy until it’s time to charge them. Most wall chargers let you refill four, maybe six, at once. Zepath’s clever solution is to ship them in an easy-to-use USB-C charging case that charges eight simultaneously. The batteries themselves are long-lasting, too.
Oura Ring 5
The Ring 5 is a fantastic entry point for new users. While short on improvements over its thicker predecessor, it’s hard not to appreciate that it manages to deliver similar battery life despite being thinner. Read our review.
007 First Light
007 First Light, a third-person stealth action game from the studio behind Hitman, is one of the best action games we’ve played this year. It features a wide variety of missions that have you sneaking through enemy territory, engaging in hand-to-hand combat, and taking part in high-speed car chases — you know, classic Bond stuff. Read our review.
Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K Plus
Amazon’s last-gen Fire TV Stick 4K Plus streams in 4K and supports Dolby Atmos, Dolby Vision, and Alexa Plus. It also ships with the redesigned Fire OS and, unlike more recent models, still lets you sideload Android TV apps.
Apple Watch Series 12
The Apple Watch Series 12 introduces AI-powered Audio Intelligence features, including sound recognition alerts, Live Rewind, and Siri Recap. It can also track your heart rate every five seconds, even when you’re not exercising, and offers faster charging than prior models. Read our review.
Fanttik S1 Pro Cordless Electric Screwdriver
Fanttik’s rechargeable electric screwdriver features three adjustable torque settings, a built-in LED light, and 16 S2 hardened steel bits for tackling everything from furniture assembly to small electronics repairs. It also comes with a magnetic storage case and supports USB-C.
Anker Laptop Power Bank
Anker’s 25,000mAh power bank sports two built-in USB-C cables (one of which is retractable), plus one USB-C and USB-A port. It tops out at 165W when charging two devices simultaneously, or 130W when charging three or four.
Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8
The cost continues to fall on Samsung’s latest, best foldable yet. The Z Fold 8 is a passport-style phone, like the iPhone Duo, with fast performance and slick design.
Nothing Ear 3A earbuds
You likely won’t find wireless earbuds with a more striking appearance than Nothing’s Ear 3A. They also sound fantastic, boast active noise cancellation, and offer robust EQ settings, making them a great pick for the price. Read our review.
Acer Swift Air 14
Acer’s answer to the MacBook Neo, with an Intel Core 5 processor, 8GB of RAM, 120Hz display, and speedy Thunderbolt 4 ports. We’re still testing this one, but it’s showing promise for an affordable choice.
Lego Project Hail Mary set
Outside of the Integrity, few spacecraft made as big a splash in 2026 as the one Ryland Grace piloted in Project Hail Mary. And now, thanks to Lego, you can construct a microscale replica of the titular Hail Mary, complete with a miniature Rocky figure.
Hoto 3.6V Electric Screwdriver Kit Pro
Hoto’s rechargeable screwdriver is ideal for small repairs. It offers three torque modes, a rotational speed of up to 220RPM, and a helpful circular LED to illuminate dark spaces. The durable case also holds all 25 steel bits and an extension bar for getting into hard-to-reach places.
Sony DualSense Wireless Controller
Sony’s DualSense Wireless Controller for the PlayStation 5 features immersive haptic feedback and resistance triggers, which feel great to use. It offers a built-in mic, a 3.5mm headphone jack, and a mute button; it also works with PC, macOS, and mobile devices via Bluetooth or USB-C.
MacBook Neo
Apple’s most affordable laptop uses the same A18 Pro chip found in the iPhone 16 Pro. It features a vibrant 13-inch display, surprisingly good speakers, and 8GB of RAM, making it a solid option for students and anyone who needs a laptop for everyday tasks. Read our review.
Ember Mug 3 (14-ounce)
Ember’s latest smart mug is designed to keep your coffee at the ideal temperature for up to three hours, with five temp settings between 120 and 145 degrees Fahrenheit. The third-gen version is similar to prior models; however, you can now adjust the heat settings directly on the mug and throw it in the dishwasher, which wasn’t the case before.
LG B6E OLED TV
Despite being an entry-level variant of the B6 OLED, this model features four HDMI 2.1 ports, a 120Hz refresh rate, a capable processor, and pixel-perfect image quality and contrast for any content you want to watch. Lower brightness is likely the biggest compromise with getting a cheaper OLED.
Alienware 32-inch 4K OLED gaming monitor
One of the most affordable Tandem RGB Stripe OLEDs is even cheaper during Black Friday. The AW3226Q monitor has a 165Hz refresh rate, G-Sync compatibility, better-looking text rendering than most other OLED monitors, and unbeatable contrast.
JBL Tour One M3
JBL’s Tour One M3 noise-canceling headphones come with a touchscreen-equipped wireless transmitter that lets you wirelessly listen to audio from in-flight entertainment systems and other devices without Bluetooth. They also offer solid active noise cancellation and last up to 70 hours on a charge.
Apple Watch Ultra 4
The latest super-rugged wearable from Apple features better battery life than the previous version, plus AI-powered features like Siri Recap also available on the Series 12.
Iniu P55-E2 Power Bank (10,000mAh)
Iniu’s P55-E2 Power Bank is an ultra-slim three-port USB charger that’s capable of fully recharging an iPhone 16 twice. It supports charging speeds of up to 45W via a USB-C port, which can deliver fast recharging for a range of gadgets.
Hisense CanvasTV (2026)
Hisense’s 2026 CanvasTV is a 4K QLED TV that doubles as wall art when you’re not watching. It features a matte, anti-glare display and runs on Google’s excellent TV software; it’s also a great pick for gamers thanks to its snappy 144Hz variable refresh rate and a pair of HDMI 2.1 ports.
Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 Combo
The Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 Combo is a beginner-friendly 3D printer that supports four filament spools. It features an enclosed build chamber, automatic bed leveling, and a large touchscreen, making it easy to produce reliable prints.
Moft Trackable Tripod Wallet
Moft’s Trackable Tripod Wallet is a MagSafe-compatible wallet that holds two cards and folds into an adjustable phone stand or small tripod. It also supports both Apple’s Find My network and Google’s Find Hub, offers Qi wireless charging, and includes a detachable shutter remote for taking photos.
Birdfy Feeder Metal 2 4K
Birdfy’s metal smart bird feeder features a wide-angle 4K camera that lets you get an up-close look at visiting birds, along with a 1.8-liter seed capacity and a built-in solar panel for charging. It also offers free AI-powered recognition of more than 6,000 bird species.
Sharge Icemag 3 Power Bank
The Icemag 3 can wirelessly deliver up to 25W of power to compatible smartphones and up to 35W wired charging via USB-C. The 10,000mAh Qi2 charger can also act as a foldable kickstand, comes with an integrated USB-C cable that serves as a lanyard, and sports a transparent design with colorful RGB lighting.
Saros
Saros is a third-person sci-fi shooter in which players fight alien enemies on a mysterious planet trapped in a time loop. The PS5 exclusive features fast-paced combat, a variety of powerful weapons, and challenging boss fights. Read our review.
Bose QuietComfort Headphones Gen 2
Bose’s second-gen QuietComfort Headphones build on the original with better sound quality and support for lossless audio over USB-C. They also offer improved noise cancellation and are more comfortable thanks to their lack of “eardrum suck.”
Dreame X60 Ultra
The Dreame X60 Ultra is a powerful robot vacuum and mop that does a great job of cleaning carpets thanks to its dual roller brushes and 35,000Pa of suction. It can climb over tall thresholds, squeeze under low furniture, and automatically detach its mop pads when vacuuming carpets.
Garmin Forerunner 265S
Garmin’s midrange Forerunner watch has an OLED display, a week’s worth of battery life, and dual-frequency GPS for better accuracy. Read our review.
Samsung The Frame (2025)
Samsung’s last-gen Frame is a 4K QLED TV that displays art on its anti-glare matte screen when not in use. It also supports Dolby Atmos, HDR10 Plus, and popular streaming apps, with refresh rates up to 144Hz on larger models.
TP-Link Tapo Matter-Certified Smart Plug Mini
TP-Link’s Wi-Fi smart plug lets you remotely control lamps, fans, and other appliances using your phone or voice commands. It supports Matter, so it works with all major smart home platforms to set schedules and timers to automatically turn devices on or off.
Pixel Buds 2a
Google’s latest pair of wireless earbuds features crisp sound, a comfortable design, and solid active noise cancellation, which is great considering the budget-friendly price tag. They even offer built-in support for Gemini and, unlike the entry-level AirPods, a purple option! Read our review.
Roku Pro Series 4K OLED TV
Roku now makes some of the most affordable yet feature-packed 4K OLED TVs available for gamers or movie lovers looking for a big TV upgrade under $1,000. The Pro Series LX with better brightness, faster refresh rate, and a polarizer to reduce reflections starts at $200 more.
Alienware AW2726DM QD-OLED monitor
If you’re on a tight budget, but want spectacular contrast and brightness control that only an OLED can provide, here’s a deal for you. Alienware’s 1440p 27-inch QD-OLED monitor with 240Hz refresh rate is selling at its lowest price yet. Read our hands-on.
Dell XPS 13 (2026)
The best XPS 13 in years. It doesn’t have a headphone jack and starts with only 8GB of RAM but it’s an excellent thin-and-light with a great screen, a solid Intel chip, and speedy storage.
Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro
Soundcore makes some of the best wireless earbuds you’ve never heard of — and the Liberty 5 Pro may be its best pair yet. The sleek buds deliver powerful noise cancellation, good sound, and surprisingly fabulous call quality for less than Apple’s latest AirPods.
Beats Powerbeats Pro 2
The latest Powerbeats Pro are a no-brainer for athletes. They pack fantastic sound and thumping bass, along with active noise cancellation, IPX4 water resistance, and heart rate monitoring. Read our review.
Logitech G Pro X2 Superstrike
The big difference between the Superstrike and other gaming mice lies beneath its main two mouse buttons. It uses haptic actuators instead of mechanical switches, allowing for lower latency and more longevity.
Yoto Mini (2024) speaker
A great first portable music player/speaker for kids. It uses insertable NFC cards (sold separately) to play music and stories to keep kiddos occupied and entertained without zoning out in front of the TV. This model supports Bluetooth and 3.5mm for private listening, too.
Nex Playground
The Nex Playground’s motion-controlled gameplay is designed for ages five and up. It comes with games like Fruit Ninja and Whack-a-Mole Deluxe, but many more titles are available via a subscription. It’s a ton of fun for kids. This is the lowest price so far in 2026. Read our review.
Apple AirPods Max (second-gen)
Nothing has changed in terms of aesthetics, but the Max 2 deliver better sound and some new features. Not exactly worth upgrading for, but fantastic for those who are considering them now. Read our full review.
Govee Uplighter Floor Lamp
It’s hard to find a cooler lamp than Govee’s Uplighter floor lamp at this price. It can light a room, and display a mesmerizing pattern up your wall and onto your ceiling.
Meta Quest 3S
The Meta Quest 3S is a battery-powered standalone VR headset that has the same chipset as the pricier Quest 3, but with the same lenses and screen resolution as the Quest 2. In addition to being able to play many games from the Meta Store, it can also be connected to a gaming PC to play VR games like Half-Life Alyx. Read our review.
Ghost of Yōtei
Sucker Punch’s follow-up to Ghost of Tsushima is everything you could want in a sequel. The open-world revenge epic brims with fluid combat and a host of welcome narrative twists, all set against the gorgeous backdrop of Japan’s Edo period. It’s precisely the type of game photo modes were made for, even if you never use them.
Beats 360 headphones
The Beats 360 are ANC headphones for people who prefer headphones over earbuds at the gym. They’re Beats’ first IP-rated cans, with ear cushions that you can easily remove for cleaning (or style points). They also stay in place during most exercises, while still delivering solid bass. Read our review.
Donkey Kong Bananza
Donkey Kong Bananza is one of the Switch 2’s first exclusive must-have titles. Its destructible environment allows you to smash your way through each of its 17 levels, and the paths you make will remain intact unless you specifically choose to reset the world. Your companion Paulene’s singing allows you to transform into animals that have abilities that allow you to reach previously inaccessible parts of levels. Read our review.
Lego Mandalorian N-1 Starfighter
Arguably the best thing to come out of The Book of Boba Fett was the Mandalorian’s N-1 Starfighter, which Lego has recreated here in miniature. It’s not quite as impressive as the 1,802-piece version, but the cheaper set still packs plenty of detail, including a spring-loaded shooter.
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
Nintendo’s latest Switch 2 exclusive is the best way to relive what is arguably the best Zelda game of all time. The revamped visuals look gorgeous, and while the game’s improved controls might annoy some purists who still cling to the heyday of ’98, we reckon most folks won’t bat an eye.
Amazon Alexa Photo Frame
A 10-inch anti-glare touchscreen that comes in a few design options. It’s a frame that features Alexa, and doubles as a smart speaker. It works with Amazon Photos, which offers unlimited storage for Prime members.
Aqara Smart Lock U400
This innovative new smart lock uses the U1 ultra-wideband (UWB) chip in many iPhones and Apple Watches to automatically unlock your door as you approach. It also works with the new Aliro standard, making it compatible with Android phones for hands-free unlocking. Read our review.
Twelve South AirFly SE
Twelve South’s entry-level Bluetooth transmitter delivers up to 25 hours of continuous use and lets you connect up to two pairs of headphones to an in-flight entertainment system, making it a great travel companion no matter where you’re going.
Catan (6th Edition)
In Catan, up to four players strategically compete and trade for resources. The iconic board game ends when one player reaches 10 “victory points,” which is achieved by constructing a sprawling civilization of roads, settlements, and cities using sheep, ore, wheat, and wood.
Control Resonant
Control Resonant is all about manipulation — of gravity, not people. Remedy’s excellent sequel to Control is an exhilarating action game, with ever-changing combat, twisted level design, and the weirdest traversal mechanics we’ve seen in a long time.
Birdbuddy Pro (solar)
Birdbuddy’s charming, camera-equipped feeder identifies and snaps shots of each bird that stops by, supplementing its 5-megapixel stills with insightful facts via an app. The solar roof helps keep the camera’s battery topped up even when it’s cloudy outside.
Azul
Azul is a game in which you arrange patterned tiles in order to create the most beautiful tapestry possible. Arranging tiles in a strategic sequence will help you build your score while limiting your opponents’ ability to grow theirs.
Magna-Tile Classic 32 Piece Set
Magna-Tiles are a quintessential kids’ toy. The colorful, semi-translucent geometric shapes are a favorite here at The Verge, especially for those of us who prefer the simplicity of building with magnets rather than bricks.
Lego Botanicals Mini Bonsai Trees set
Lego’s 709-piece kit lets you construct three brick-ified bonsai trees, including a black pine, a ginkgo with yellow leaves, and a wisteria with hanging lilac flowers. It also comes with three ornamental displays, just in case you want a raised stand on which to showcase them.
Sonos Beam (Gen 2)
The Beam isn’t as powerful as the Sonos Arc, nor can it match the flagship soundbar’s Dolby Atmos immersion bubble. But you still get room-filling surround sound for less money — and the Beam ties into the Sonos ecosystem for added convenience. Read our review.
Google Pixel 11 Pro
Google wants to sell you on the Pro’s software features, but it’s the underlying hardware that makes it a stellar Android handset. The build quality is incredible, the larger telephoto sensor is an improvement, and it now supports faster wired speeds and Qi2.2 for up to 25W wireless charging. Read our review.
Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Flow
Roborock’s first roller-mop robot vacuum, the Curv 2 Flow, features flagship specs at a midrange price, including excellent mopping, a retractable mop cover, 20,000Pa suction, AI-powered obstacle avoidance, and a compact design. Read our review.
Insta360 Link 2
The Insta360 Link 2 offers the same auto-swiveling design as its excellent predecessor, only in a smaller form factor. It also offers a slate of new features, including group tracking and no-follow zones.
CMF Buds 2A
With 12.4mm drivers, active noise cancellation, and an IP54 rating, the CMF Buds 2A offer high-end features at an affordable price. You can also customize the sound, adjust ANC levels, and find the earbuds using the Nothing X app.
Philips Hue Festavia string lights
These smart lights have beautiful colors, a nice selection of festive scenes, and an easy-to-use app. They are super reliable when paired with a Hue Bridge and also work over Bluetooth. They come in three lengths, work with all the major smart home platforms, and are Matter-compatible. Read our review.
Echo Dot Max
The Echo Dot Max features a flat design and a redesigned sound system, which delivers nearly three times the bass as its predecessor. It also offers improved conversation detection and better noise filtering, thanks to Amazon’s new AZ3 chip. Read our review.
Glocusent Bookmark Style Reading Light
Glocusent’s clip-in reading light features five brightness levels and multiple color temperature settings, ranging from a soft, warm glow that’s great for late-night reading to a brighter light that’s perfect for daytime use. The slim USB light easily slips into your pocket, too, so you can read anywhere, from a cozy bed to a dimly lit train.
Vantage
Vantage isn’t your typical open-world exploration game. It’s a sci-fi roguelike that has you traversing an alien planet alongside up to five players, each of whom must solve puzzles and complete their mission before their time, morale, or health runs out. It’s not as charming as Stonemaier’s award-winning Wingspan, but it is far more interesting.
SwitchBot Standing Circulator Fan
A quiet, battery-powered fan that moves a lot of air despite its small size, the Switchbot Standing Circulator is a surprisingly versatile smart home addition.
JBL Go 4
The last-gen JBL Go 4 has been around for a bit, but the pocket-sized Bluetooth speaker still delivers with up to seven hours of runtime, dual-device connectivity, and an IP67 rating for water and dust resistance. You can also pair it with other Go 4 speakers for bigger stereo sound, if desired.
Fairphone 6 Plus
Fairphone’s latest is a very light update to the 6, adding a newer processor and carrying forward its repairability and ethical values. Tradeoffs compared to a traditional smartphone are few, and the benefits are real.
Ugreen Nexode 240W USB-C Cable with Digital Display
The proliferation of miniature screens continues with Ugreen’s latest Nexode USB-C Cable, which features a full-color LCD screen on one end that displays current power draw (up to 240W). It also supports 480Mbps data transfer speeds and, unlike similar power meter-equipped cables, lets you turn off the screen when needed.
Apple Watch SE 3
The Apple Watch SE 3 is a major glow-up, adding an always-on display, wrist-temperature sensor, a more powerful processor, and fast charging. Read our review.
Pokémon Pokopia
Nintendo’s latest Pokémon spinoff for the Switch 2 is part Pokémon, part Minecraft, and part Animal Crossing. Yet, despite borrowing gameplay mechanics from each, the cozy life sim is more than the sum of its expansive, building-centric parts. It’s breezy and warm-hearted, with enough secrets to keep mother dearest occupied for hours on end.
Google Pixel 10A
Google’s new Pixel 10A introduces faster wired charging, Satellite SOS, and new AI tools like Camera Coach and Auto Best Take. Otherwise, it’s basically the Pixel 9A, with the same Tensor G4 chip and a dual-camera system. Read our review.
Asus ProArt P14 (RTX Spark)
The entry-point into RTX Spark laptops, the Asus ProArt is a creator-focused MacBook Pro wannabe with a sleek blacked-out design and lovely OLED display. Read our initial Nvidia RTX Spark hands-on.
Fractal Scape gaming headset
There are many gaming headsets out there, but few as elegant as Fractal’s Scape. The PC-focused (but Switch- and PlayStation-compatible) wireless headset offer great sound and include a wireless charger, and they have easy-to-master physical controls.
Nintendo eShop gift cards
Everyone knows gift cards aren’t the best gift, but with such steep discounts happening on Nintendo eShop credit, you can save a lot on a Switch 2, or games and accessories, if you’re alright with jumping through a couple extra hoops.
Xreal One Pro AR glasses
USB-C display glasses can make travel (or relaxing on the couch) more fun by putting a huge virtual screen in front of your face. Xreal’s One Pro are some of the best out there at displaying content from your phone, tablet, laptop, or portable handheld.
Govee Permanent Outdoor Lights 2
Govee’s Permanent Outdoor Lights 2 are Matter-ready smart lights you can leave up year-round. They can display multiple colors at once, with 100 preset lighting scenes, customizable effects, and the ability to sync to music. The lights also feature an IP67 rating for dust and water resistance.
Ecobee Smart Thermostat Premium
The Ecobee Smart Thermostat Premium is an excellent option for adding smarts and some style to your HVAC system. As well as being a smart way to control your energy use, the thermostat can also act as a video intercom for Ecobee’s excellent doorbell camera and an indoor air quality monitor. Read our review.
Cricut Joy 2
The Cricut Joy 2 is a small crafting machine designed for smaller projects, including custom cards, stickers, vinyl decals, labels, bookmarks, and iron-ons. It can cut designs up to 4.5 inches wide and brings Cricut’s Print Then Cut feature to its entry-level lineup. Read our review.
Apple Pencil (USB-C)
Apple’s entry-level stylus attaches magnetically to supported iPads, though it doesn’t support magnetic charging. Instead, you pair and charge it by connecting it to your device’s USB-C port. It includes tilt sensitivity and Apple Pencil Hover support, but it doesn’t offer double-tap gestures or pressure sensitivity.
Amazon Echo Time
Although it’s not Amazon’s first bedside alarm clock, the Echo Time is focused on helping you sleep better. The camera-less Alexa speaker can detect your sleep stage via ultrasound and use smart alarms to ease you into the day, but only if you want it to.
Update, November 27th: Updated to include several new picks, including those for the Cricut Joy 2, Apple Pencil (USB-C), and the Echo Time.

articles.title: Our 2027 Innovators Under 35 competition is now open
articles.text:
Our 2027 Innovators Under 35 competition is now open
Nominate yourself or someone you know by January 19.
Every year, the editors at MIT Technology Review select 35 of the world’s top young scientists, entrepreneurs, and inventors to honor as our newest class of Innovators Under 35. And starting today, our 2027 competition is officially open for nominations.
We’re on the hunt for researchers and founders who are engineering solutions to some of the most formidable problems society faces, including human disease and climate change. We also recognize those who have made clever and useful inventions, important new scientific discoveries, or technological breakthroughs early in their careers.
We want to hear about people, based anywhere in the world, who are responsible for a major finding or advance and can show real-world impact from their work. To qualify for the list, a nominee must be under the age of 35 as of October 1, 2027 (that is, born on or after October 2, 1992).
Have someone in mind? Or think you’d be a great candidate and want to nominate yourself? Follow this link to suggest someone who you think should make our 2027 list. It’s free and takes only a few minutes. Just be sure to get your nomination in before the deadline—which is 11:59 p.m. Eastern time on Tuesday, January 19.
After the deadline, our editors will review all nominees and select a group of semifinalists, whom we’ll invite to complete a formal application. Then, dozens of expert judges will help us evaluate those applicants and settle on the finalists. You can read more about our selection process here.
Our newsroom began producing our Innovators Under 35 list in 1999. It’s an annual exercise that helps our reporters scout out the brightest young minds in the fields they cover. It also introduces our audience to dozens of rising stars worth watching in the years to come. Subscribers can explore the 2026 list and peruse the full archives.
We look forward to reviewing your nominations.

Interspecies communication
Decoding how animals communicate could reveal the inner lives of other species—and give humans a window onto how they see the world.

Deploying simple, proven methods for making our roads safer could save more than 1 million lives worldwide each year.

Trevor Wischnewsky is making sure that the sky stays organized as we enter the age of food delivery by drone.

articles.title: OpenAI contra-ataca e acusa Apple de roubar segredos comerciais
articles.text:
A OpenAI abriu uma nova frente na disputa judicial com a Apple. Nesta sexta-feira (27), a empresa responsável pelo ChatGPT apresentou uma ação contra a fabricante do iPhone, acusando-a de roubar segredos comerciais e dificultar seu acesso a fornecedores de hardware.
A iniciativa é uma contraofensiva depois que a Apple processou a OpenAI e dois ex-funcionários, alegando apropriação indevida de informações confidenciais para beneficiar os planos da criadora do ChatGPT no mercado de dispositivos eletrônicos.
As novas alegações foram apresentadas em um tribunal federal da Califórnia (EUA). Segundo a OpenAI, as práticas de contratação da Apple foram planejadas para “prender” funcionários e impedir que trabalhassem no desenvolvimento de tecnologias concorrentes.
Disputa começou com acusações da Apple
A tensão entre as empresas aumentou depois que a Apple entrou com uma ação judicial contra a OpenAI e dois antigos funcionários. A fabricante acusou a concorrente de se apropriar de segredos comerciais para favorecer sua entrada no mercado de hardware para consumidores. A OpenAI negou as acusações. Agora, a empresa apresenta suas próprias alegações, ampliando o confronto jurídico entre as duas gigantes da tecnologia.
A disputa ocorre em meio à intensificação da corrida pelo desenvolvimento de produtos de inteligência artificial (IA), que também envolve a competição por profissionais especializados e tecnologias proprietárias.
Leia mais:
- Apple prepara iPhone 18e, novo iPad e MacBook Neo para 2027
- Ex-funcionário da OpenAI acusado de espionagem será solto com fiança milionária
- OpenAI corrige erro no GPT-6.2 e muda limites de uso dos planos
Briga pode envolver o futuro dos dispositivos de IA
Além das acusações sobre segredos comerciais e contratação de funcionários, o processo coloca em evidência uma disputa estratégica pelo controle dos futuros dispositivos de IA.
Esses aparelhos poderão funcionar sem depender dos aplicativos e sistemas operacionais tradicionais que dominam atualmente o mercado de tecnologia.
Segundo a Reuters, analistas acreditam que a OpenAI está trabalhando no desenvolvimento de um telefone ou outro dispositivo próprio. Caso produtos desse tipo tenham sucesso, poderão desviar parte da atenção dos consumidores do iPhone, principal produto da Apple.
A disputa judicial, portanto, vai além de uma divergência entre duas empresas. Ela também envolve a concorrência por tecnologias e plataformas que poderão definir a próxima geração de dispositivos eletrônicos.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: WhatsApp acaba de solucionar uno de los mayores dolores de cabeza al viajar
articles.text:
WhatsApp anunció una nueva función que les facilitará la vida a las personas que viajan mucho. La popular aplicación de mensajería permitirá comprar una tarjeta eSIM directamente desde la aplicación. Los usuarios ya no tendrán que preocuparse por buscar un kiosco o un operador en el aeropuerto, ya que tendrán conexión de datos en automático.
De acuerdo con una publicación en el blog oficial, WhatsApp permitirá comprar e instalar una eSIM sin salir de la aplicación. La empresa no ofrece detalles específicos sobre el funcionamiento de esta característica, solamente que adquirirla "será tan fácil como enviar un mensaje". Una vez que la compres, podrás usar WhatsApp con tu mismo número de siempre, evitándote el problema de tener que activar otra cuenta.
WhatsApp mencionó que están trabajando con proveedores de e-SIM y socios de telecomunicaciones, entre los que se encuentran Jio, Smart Axiata, Smart Communications, Verizon y otros. La función se activará en algunos países y se expandirá de forma gradual, por lo que los usuarios no tendrán que hacer nada, solo esperar la notificación de que ya está disponible dentro de la app.
"Personas de todo el mundo confían en WhatsApp cuando viajan", dijo la compañía. "Así es como obtienen su tarjeta de embarque antes de salir, coordinan su recogida cuando arriban y avisan a la familia que han llegado bien".
La nueva función de comprar una eSIM dentro de WhatsApp puede caer como un jarro de agua fría para las empresas que se dedican a vender tarjetas para viajeros. Hasta hace unos años, este era un negocio redondo en los aeropuertos o terminales de trenes, donde pequeños kioscos ofrecían tarjetas SIM con datos. Lamentablemente, muchas de estas compañías tienen planes poco atractivos, pero son la opción más fácil para no depender del Wi-Fi.
WhatsApp sigue añadiendo nuevas funciones en su actualización más reciente
Además de las tarjetas eSIM, WhatsApp implementó una función que permite programar mensajes. Esta característica habilita la opción de enviar mensajes de forma diferida para gestionar mejor nuestras comunicaciones. Si tienes que contactar a alguien a cierta hora, ya no necesitas programar un recordatorio; solo basta con elegir la fecha y hora en que quieres que se entregue y WhatsApp se encargará del resto.
Los mensajes se pueden programar en un lapso que va de los 10 minutos a los 14 días después de su creación. El usuario solo necesita dejar pulsado el botón de enviar para que aparezca una ventana emergente en la que se elige el horario de entrega. La persona que está del otro lado del chat no sabrá que se trata de un mensaje programado, ya que los recibirán como si acabaras de enviarlos.
La buena noticia es que esta función aplica para mensajes con texto, fotos y vídeos. Por ahora no hay detalles sobre la posibilidad de enviar audios programados, así que si las notas de voz son lo tuyo, tendrás que esperar. El resto solo necesita actualizar la app a la versión más reciente y comenzar a usar los mensajes programados a partir de hoy.

articles.title: U.S. MATCH Act Puts Semiconductor Inspection in Focus- EE Times
articles.text:
Printing an advanced transistor and manufacturing a commercially viable chip are two very different achievements. The distinction deserves greater attention in Washington’s semiconductor export control debate.
On Nov. 25, Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen confirmed during a visit to Beijing that his government was working to prevent the passage of the proposed U.S. MATCH Act. While the immediate dispute centers on ASML and immersion deep ultraviolet (DUV) lithography, the legislation raises a broader question: How much of China’s manufacturing capability depends on foreign equipment that measures and controls production rather than creates semiconductor structures?
As transistor architectures and advanced packaging become more complex, the answer increasingly lies in metrology and inspection.
The economics of yield
Gate-all-around (GAA) transistors require precise control of nanosheet dimensions, epitaxial layer thickness, and material composition. Small variations can affect threshold voltage, carrier mobility, and device performance. Advanced packaging introduces additional challenges, particularly in surface preparation, bonding alignment, and interconnect integrity.
Consider a simplified assembly containing eight known-good dies and requiring seven bonding operations. Assuming independent bonding outcomes, a 99% yield per operation produces a cumulative bonding yield of approximately 93%. At 97%, it falls to 81%, even before accounting for other manufacturing losses.
A defect introduced during final assembly can compromise several functional dies and the manufacturing value accumulated across multiple processing stages. Detecting defects before bonding becomes increasingly valuable as the number and cost of dies within a package rise. This makes process-control equipment a strategic manufacturing asset alongside lithography.
The physics behind process control
Two Israeli equipment manufacturers, Nova and Camtek, illustrate how these capabilities are distributed across the global semiconductor ecosystem.
Nova’s Metrion platform, adopted by leading logic and memory manufacturers for GAA and advanced DRAM applications, uses secondary ion mass spectrometry (SIMS). An ion beam removes material from a sample, and the resulting secondary ions are analyzed to characterize composition at different depths.
Conventional optical dimensional measurements can characterize geometry, but advanced transistor structures also require information about elemental composition and material interfaces beneath the surface. Integrating SIMS into production environments helps manufacturers identify material variations before they translate into electrical performance problems.
Camtek addresses a different manufacturing constraint. Its Hawk platform supports inspection and three-dimensional metrology for advanced packaging, including wafers containing more than 500 million bumps at pitches below 10 micrometers.
Higher optical resolution typically narrows the field of view in a given imaging configuration, increasing the number of images required to inspect a wafer. Three-dimensional measurements introduce the additional challenge of reconstructing surface topography to identify height variations and planarity issues. Manufacturers must balance sensitivity, measurement accuracy, and throughput. An inspection system that cannot keep pace with production becomes a capacity constraint, regardless of its laboratory performance.
Washington’s 150-day clock
The Senate version of the MATCH Act, S.4281, establishes a mechanism for identifying critical manufacturing equipment and coordinating restrictions with allied supplier countries.
Within 150 days of enactment, the Commerce Department would be required to issue regulations and assess whether allied suppliers’ governments had adopted equivalent controls. Subject to the bill’s waiver provisions, failed diplomatic efforts could trigger unilateral U.S. restrictions on covered foreign equipment through expanded foreign direct product rules.
For Israel, the implications are tangible. If Israeli export controls fall short of the proposed requirements, Washington could extend its jurisdiction to qualifying foreign-produced equipment. Israeli suppliers such as Nova and Camtek would then face potential licensing restrictions based on equipment classification, technology provenance, customer identity, and end use.
Camtek generated approximately 49% of its 2025 revenue from China. The figure underscores how deeply international process-control suppliers are commercially intertwined with China’s semiconductor expansion.
The bill’s annual review mechanism adds another dimension: Equipment categories that escape restrictions today could come under scrutiny as manufacturing technologies evolve.
Controlling installed capacity
Perhaps the most consequential provision concerns servicing.
Semiconductor equipment requires periodic calibration, replacement parts, software maintenance, and application engineering. Introducing new materials or device architectures often requires additional measurement recipes and qualification work.
Inspection algorithms must also adapt to changing defect characteristics, surface reflectivity, and structural complexity. Restrictions on technical support could consequently affect equipment utilization and the qualification of new processes, even where manufacturers already possess the necessary hardware.
Restricting new shipments limits capacity expansion. Restricting support can undermine the productivity of capital already deployed.
China’s learning opportunity
The policy dilemma is particularly acute in inspection and metrology, where competitive advantage depends partly on accumulated production experience.
Chinese equipment developers such as Skyverse need sophisticated optics, precision motion systems, and advanced algorithms. They also need exposure to real manufacturing variability, representative defect populations, and feedback from production engineers.
If export restrictions encourage Chinese manufacturers such as SMIC and CXMT to qualify domestic equipment more extensively, local suppliers could gain access to precisely the environments required to improve measurement repeatability, defect classification, and equipment reliability. Each qualification cycle creates opportunities to refine hardware, software, and process recipes. Access to live production lines is itself a competitive asset.
Washington must weigh the immediate benefits of restricting established process-control technologies against the possibility of accelerating the development of competing Chinese platforms.
In inspection and metrology, restricting equipment exports may buy Washington time. But giving Chinese fabs a stronger incentive to train domestic equipment suppliers on live production lines could substantially shorten the time it actually gains.

articles.title: Un ingeniero químico muestra cómo limpiar el inodoro de forma correcta: “Te voy a mostrar lo que he aprendido sobre cómo limpiar correctamente el inodoro”
articles.text:
Si eres de los que echa un buen chorro de lejía al inodoro y después pasa la escobilla, puede que estés saltándote un paso importante. Diego, un ingeniero químico que comparte consejos en Instagram (@renovandoconideas), ha explicado cómo limpiar el váter y por qué utilizar más productos no significa conseguir una limpieza mejor.
En realidad, lo primero que recomienda es bastante sencillo: retirar la suciedad visible antes de desinfectar. Así lo explica también el artículo publicado por Clarín, que recoge sus consejos y las indicaciones de los Centros para el Control y la Prevención de Enfermedades (CDC) de Estados Unidos.
El error de mezclar productos para limpiar el váter
Para empezar, utiliza un limpiador adecuado para el baño y frota las zonas donde haya suciedad. Después tendrás que aclarar los restos del producto siguiendo sus instrucciones. Si necesitas desinfectar, aplica un desinfectante compatible con la superficie y respeta el tiempo que indica el fabricante. No sirve de mucho retirarlo antes de que haya actuado.
Pero hay una advertencia especialmente importante: nunca mezcles lejía con vinagre, amoniaco ni otros limpiadores. Algunas combinaciones pueden desprender gases tóxicos, así que tampoco conviene echar lejía directamente en un inodoro donde todavía quedan restos de otro producto. Además, es recomendable mantener el baño ventilado mientras limpias.
¿Y hay que desinfectarlo absolutamente todo cada día? No necesariamente. Los CDC explican que, en condiciones domésticas habituales, limpiar con agua y detergente suele ser suficiente para eliminar buena parte de los gérmenes. La desinfección cobra especial importancia cuando alguien está enfermo o convive en casa una persona con mayor riesgo de infección.

En Decoesfera | Cristina Etxeberria, experta en limpieza: "La lejía no limpia, desinfecta, y no es lo mismo"

articles.title: Moins de 100 euros pour un robot aspirateur-laveur, c'est possible grâce au Black Friday et à Xiaomi
articles.text:
Les robots aspirateurs-laveurs ont inondé le marché depuis plusieurs années. Vous pouvez en trouver pour tous les prix, mais difficilement pour moins de 100 euros sans que l’engin en question fasse de concessions. Le Xiaomi Robot Vacuum S40 passe sous cette barre ce vendredi 27 novembre : pour le Black Friday, il est vendu à moitié prix par son constructeur.
Pourquoi aspirer avec le Xiaomi Robot Vacuum S40 ?
- Pour ses quatre modes d’aspiration et une puissance maximale de 10 000 Pa
- Pour l’application qui offre un nettoyage personnalisé
- Pour son autonomie annoncée de 180 minutes (en mode standard)
Pendant le Black Friday, Xiaomi divise par deux le prix de son Robot Vacuum S40. Il est actuellement affiché à 99,99 euros au lieu de 199,99 euros.
Un aspirateur robot polyvalent
Le Xiaomi Robot Vacuum S40 propose quatre modes d’aspiration (silencieux, standard, fort et turbo) adaptés à la quantité de poussières, poils et autres miettes présents sur le sol. Il atteint 10 000 Pa d’aspiration au maximum, en mode turbo. Attention, plus la puissance demandée sera importante, plus la batterie du robot se videra rapidement. Xiaomi annonce une autonomie de 180 minutes, mais ce chiffre est mesuré en mode standard, sur du carrelage. En mode fort ou turbo, comptez moins.
Successeur du Saros 10R annoncé en début d’année, le Saros 20 Set passe de 1 299 à 799 euros. C’est l’une des meilleures affaires du Black Friday pour s’offrir la nouveauté à petit prix !
Cet aspirateur robot possède deux brosses (une principale et une latérale), toutes les deux équipées d’un système anti-emmêlement. La brosse principale a des picots qui limitent l’emmêlement des poils et des longs cheveux.
Une fois que le Xiaomi Robot Vacuum S40 aura aspiré tout ce qu’il y a sur votre sol, place au lavage. L’engin possède un réservoir d’eau de 270 ml. Avant son passage, vous choisissez dans l’application entre trois niveaux de débit d’eau.
Un nettoyage selon vos envies
Ce débit d’eau n’est pas le seul élément personnalisable de ce Xiaomi Robot Vacuum S40. Pour cartographier votre intérieur, le robot s’appuie sur une navigation laser LDS, et il sait enregistrer des cartes sur plusieurs étages. Une fois la carte prête, place à la programmation de ses passages ! Grâce à l’application Xiaomi Home, vous pourrez définir des zones interdites ou des murs virtuels que ce robot aspirateur évitera. Ce modèle est aussi compatible avec Amazon Alexa et l’Assistant Google. Un simple « OK Google, lance le nettoyage » suffira pour mettre en route le produit de Xiaomi.
Dans une même pièce, il est possible de personnaliser le nettoyage. Vous pouvez demander au Xiaomi Robot Vacuum S40 de passer sur le sol, mais d’éviter les tapis et inversement. Attention, Xiaomi précise dans sa FAQ que le robot ne reconnaît pas les tapis tout seul : il faut donc les indiquer vous-même dans l’application.
Si vous disposez de seuils, pas d’inquiétude puisque l’aspirateur robot peut franchir des pas de porte jusqu’à 20 mm, à condition que sa lavette soit sèche, précise Xiaomi. Une fois qu’il aura fini ses missions, il rejoindra automatiquement sa station de recharge. Pour ce prix, il n’y a logiquement pas de station d’entretien.
Le Xiaomi Robot Vacuum S40 est l’un des aspirateurs robots les plus abordables du moment, mais si vous voulez découvrir d’autres modèles, c’est possible grâce à notre guide des meilleurs robots aspirateurs.

articles.title: « Tant qu’on en tire encore quelque chose » : un économiste propose de vendre Volkswagen à la Chine
articles.text:
Volkswagen traverse sa plus mauvaise passe depuis le Dieselgate. Le 29 octobre, le groupe a annoncé une perte d’exploitation de 5,9 milliards d’euros sur le troisième trimestre 2026, alors qu’il commence à appliquer le plan d’austérité le plus radical de son histoire. Forcément, la crise du groupe alimente les spéculations.
Moritz Schularick, président de l’Institut de Kiel pour l’économie mondiale (IfW), en a avancé une pour le moins radicale ce mardi 24 novembre. À Berlin, lors d’une conférence sur l’industrie organisée par le ministère fédéral de l’Économie, le BDI (l’organisation patronale de l’industrie) et le syndicat IG Metall, il a suggéré de vendre aux Chinois « un certain groupe à Wolfsburg » (on se demande bien lequel), « tant qu’on peut encore en tirer quelque chose ». Selon le Handelsblatt, il estimait que ce ne serait « pas une mauvaise idée ».
Une manière de conserver la valeur ajoutée en Allemagne, vraiment ?
Pour l’économiste, ce qui compte, c’est que « la valeur ajoutée et la production restent ici ». « À qui appartient la production au bout du compte, c’est secondaire », a-t-il ajouté. Selon le Handelsblatt, ses propos ont fait murmurer la salle, d’autant que Michael Jansen, qui dirige la représentation de Volkswagen à Berlin, était dans le public.
Moritz Schularick estime que l’Allemagne est désormais un « pays en développement » face à la Chine sur ce marché. Il veut donc que l’Europe laisse entrer les voitures chinoises, mais qu’elle pousse leurs fabricants à produire sur place, avec des aides réservées au « Made in Europe » ou des coentreprises obligatoires. Pékin a appliqué cette même recette aux constructeurs étrangers pendant des décennies, à commencer par Volkswagen, associé à SAIC depuis 1984.
L’économiste n’en est pas à son coup d’essai
Moritz Schularick a reçu en 2022 le prix Leibniz, la principale récompense scientifique allemande, pour ses travaux sur les crises financières. Ses propos sont donc écoutés, mais ils font souvent polémique chez ses pairs.
En décembre 2024, il parlait déjà d’« erreurs de management » chez les trois constructeurs allemands (BMW, Mercedes et Volkswagen), et doutait qu’un groupe « un peu lourd » comme VW rattrape vite son retard sur l’électrique grand public.
En novembre 2025, à la télévision allemande, il prédisait que VW, BMW et Mercedes ne seraient probablement plus sous leur forme actuelle en 2030. Les constructeurs chinois ne sont pas à l’abri pour autant : leur industrie traverse elle aussi une sévère sélection.
Début juillet 2026, dans un entretien à la Süddeutsche Zeitung, il jugeait même « probable » un rachat de VW par un constructeur chinois, en citant BYD comme exemple. À l’époque, un porte-parole de Volkswagen avait répondu à Auto Motor und Sport que le groupe ne commentait pas des « spéculations sans fondement ».
À Berlin, l’économiste est donc passé de la prédiction à la recommandation. Il faut tout de même prendre l’hypothèse d’un Volkswagen chinois avec de grosses pincettes : aucun acheteur n’a fait d’offre et aucune discussion de rachat n’a été rapportée.
BYD, seul acheteur imaginable ?
Sur le papier, BYD serait le candidat le plus plausible. Le constructeur de Shenzhen a déjà essayé deux fois d’entrer au capital de Renault, en 2024 puis à l’automne 2025. Une source évoquait même « une volonté de prendre le contrôle », avaient révélé Les Échos en juillet 2026. Renault aurait dit non les deux fois, avec l’État français, qui détient environ 30 % des droits de vote.
Chez Volkswagen, le verrou est encore plus difficile à faire sauter. La holding des familles Porsche et Piëch détient la majorité des droits de vote (53,3 %), tandis que le Land de Basse-Saxe en possède 20 %. Autant dire qu’un éventuel rachat ne se ferait pas sans l’accord de ces deux actionnaires.
Volkswagen a pourtant encore des raisons d’espérer. Malgré près de 8 milliards d’euros de charges exceptionnelles au troisième trimestre, son résultat opérationnel aurait été positif, à hauteur de 1,9 milliard d’euros, sans ces dépenses. La marque Volkswagen a également signé un record de livraisons de voitures électriques et hybrides rechargeables en Chine en octobre, avec plus de 28 000 unités. Des signes encourageants, même si le constructeur allemand est encore loin d’avoir réglé tous ses problèmes.

articles.title: Researcher finds unprotected database with about 2 billion credentials, the largest he's ever seen
articles.text:
Ripple effect: Ethical security researcher Jeremiah Fowler recently uncovered a massive unsecured database containing around two billion potentially compromised account credentials. A single database was apparently hosting several collections of account credentials from multiple security incidents, and anyone could download the data before the host decided to block access.
Fowler said that the database he discovered was neither protected by a password nor encrypted in any way. Around 2 billion credentials were just sitting there, waiting for someone to grab the data and use it to launch further attacks against users. The dataset included email addresses, logins and other user IDs, passwords, and more.
The researcher probed the online database by reviewing the neatly organized data, finding additional content types such as application credentials, browser passwords, cookies, session tokens, and other "identifiers." Fowler said that this was the largest collection of compromised accounts he had ever found. The dataset was more than 13 times bigger than an exposure he previously reported and included a lot more device-specific data for potential attackers to exploit.
The database was also noteworthy for how the plaintext data was organized in thousands of different folders, with some documents grouped by country-code top-level domain. Around 400,000 documents appeared to come from advanced malware threats, as they were stored in separate folders focused on individual victims.
Based on the data he personally reviewed, Fowler provided an estimation of the services and domains that were most affected by the breach. The researcher remarked that the compromised accounts might have appeared in multiple documents, which means the database may include several duplicate accounts. Furthermore, the users likely own multiple accounts on different online services.
Fowler provided no definitive explanation for the origin of the dataset. The account collection might have come from multiple malware operations and later been stored in a single archive to be sold through underground marketplaces. The database could even be part of a large, legitimate security operation by other researchers or law enforcement agencies, with experts trying to identify and notify victims or monitor suspected criminal marketplaces.
The researcher did not provide any specific information about where the data archive was stored or which company was hosting it. He only said that he reported the breach to the hosting provider, which took a few days to finally restrict public access. While he did not download any data, Fowler had plenty of time to run queries and make a few estimations.
Massive databases containing billions of potentially compromised accounts are nothing new, and users are contributing to the ever-growing infostealing threat by not following proper opsec when they access online resources. Fowler warned that users should avoid installing unknown browser extensions, downloading unsolicited email attachments, or clicking links in suspicious messages. As the mega-database he discovered clearly demonstrates, sometimes resetting passwords is not enough to stay in the clear. In a worst-case scenario, worried users should consider factory resetting their devices before adopting secure authentication solutions such as password managers or multi-factor authentication.

articles.title: Final de la Copa Libertadores 2026 por Futbol Libre y Roja Directa: por qué evitarlo
articles.text:
Este sábado 28 de noviembre de 2026, Palmeiras y Estudiantes de La Plata disputarán la final de la Copa Libertadores en el Estadio Centenario de Montevideo. La magnitud del encuentro concentra millones de búsquedas simultáneas en Sudamérica, impulsando a una parte de la audiencia hacia portales de retransmisión no autorizados como Futbol Libre y Roja Directa.
A diferencia de las aplicaciones piratas que requieren instalación en el teléfono, estos sitios operan directamente desde el navegador web, exponiendo tanto a computadoras como a dispositivos móviles a vectores de ataque diseñados para vulnerar la privacidad y el sistema operativo.
Malvertising y capas invisibles (Clickjacking)
Ni Futbol Libre ni Roja Directa alojan señales de televisión propias; su infraestructura consiste en indexar enlaces de terceros y monetizar el tráfico mediante redes de publicidad maliciosa (malvertising). Para maximizar los clics forzados, los reproductores de video integrados en estas páginas están cubiertos por capas transparentes (clickjacking).
Al intentar iniciar la transmisión del partido, quitar el silencio o ampliar la pantalla, el usuario es redirigido automáticamente a dominios externos. Estas páginas emergentes suelen simular alertas del sistema operativo que exigen descargar supuestos códecs de video, actualizaciones de reproductores o extensiones obligatorias para ver la final. En la práctica, estos archivos son ejecutables maliciosos (troyanos o adware) que comprometen la seguridad local apenas se abren.
Secuestro del navegador y campañas de phishing
Una práctica habitual en los espejos y clones de Futbol Libre y Roja Directa consiste en bloquear la señal del partido detrás de un aviso falso que solicita “verificar que no es un robot” activando las notificaciones del navegador (Chrome, Edge o Safari).
Al conceder este permiso, el portal adquiere la capacidad de enviar ventanas emergentes directamente al escritorio de la computadora o a la barra de notificaciones del celular, incluso después de finalizar el encuentro y cerrar la pestaña. Estas alertas imitan advertencias de virus detectados (scareware) o avisos de entidades bancarias, buscando dirigir a la víctima hacia formularios de phishing para capturar contraseñas y datos de tarjetas de crédito.
Cryptojacking sostenido durante el partido
Una final de Copa Libertadores garantiza un tiempo mínimo de permanencia de 90 minutos, con la posibilidad de extenderse a tiempo suplementario y tanda de penales. Los operadores de estos portales aprovechan la larga duración de la pestaña activa para ejecutar secuencias de código (scripts) de cryptojacking en segundo plano.
Mientras se desarrolla el partido entre Palmeiras y Estudiantes, el navegador utiliza de forma oculta los recursos del procesador (CPU) y la tarjeta gráfica (GPU) del dispositivo para minar criptomonedas a favor de terceros. Esto se traduce en un calentamiento excesivo del equipo, activación constante de los ventiladores, bloqueos en otras aplicaciones y un desgaste acelerado de la batería.
Protocolo de limpieza tras ingresar a estos portales
Si accedió a enlaces de Futbol Libre o Roja Directa y aceptó permisos emergentes, descargó archivos o experimentó redirecciones sospechosas, ejecute de inmediato el siguiente protocolo de mitigación:
- Revocación de permisos en el navegador: Ingrese a la configuración de Privacidad y Seguridad de su navegador web, diríjase al apartado de “Configuración de sitios” y elimine todos los permisos de notificaciones, ventanas emergentes o ubicación asignados a dominios desconocidos.
- Eliminación de descargas y extensiones: Revise la carpeta de Descargas del equipo y borre cualquier archivo ejecutable reciente (.exe, .apk, .dmg, .zip) que no haya descargado de forma consciente. Verifique también la lista de extensiones del navegador y desinstale aquellas que no reconozca.
- Escaneo con software de seguridad: Ejecute un análisis completo del sistema operativo utilizando Microsoft Defender o un antivirus actualizado para detectar y aislar troyanos, adware o scripts persistentes.
- Verificación de procesos activos: Cierre completamente el navegador y abra el Administrador de tareas (en Windows) o el Monitor de actividad (en macOS). Compruebe que el consumo de CPU se mantenga en niveles normales de reposo para descartar procesos ocultos de criptominería.
